q: 设计 Instagram 时，三条核心功能需求是？
q_en: When designing Instagram, what are the three core functional requirements?
options: 发帖（照片/视频+说明）；关注用户；按时间倒序看 feed
发帖并允许点赞评论互动；支持搜索用户、话题和地点
关注用户；发布短时效的 Stories；开通实时直播功能
发帖；关注用户；查看由机器学习排序模型按兴趣个性化打分的 feed
options_en: Create posts with photos or video and a caption; follow users; view a chronological feed.
Create posts with likes and comments; support searching users, hashtags, and locations.
Follow users; publish ephemeral Stories; enable real-time live streaming.
Create posts; follow users; view a feed scored and personalized by a machine-learning ranking model.
why: 核心三条：发帖、关注、看时间序 feed。点赞评论、搜索、Stories、直播、算法排序都被划到范围外。
why_en: The three core requirements are creating posts, following users, and viewing a chronological feed from followed users.
optionExplanations: 这三项就是范围内的核心功能：发帖、关注、按时间倒序看 feed。
点赞评论和搜索是后续迭代的互动/发现功能，题目明确划在范围外。
Stories 和直播是独立的内容形态，需要额外的存储和流媒体架构，不在这轮范围内。
按机器学习排序的个性化 feed 是推荐系统能力，题目要的是时间倒序，不是算法排序。
optionExplanations_en: These three are the in-scope core: posting, following, and a chronological feed.
Likes/comments and search are later engagement/discovery features, explicitly out of scope here.
Stories and live streaming are separate content formats needing their own storage and streaming stack — not this round.
A ranking-model feed is a recommendation-system capability; the requirement asks for chronological, not ranked.
scenario: 面试只有 45 分钟设计 Instagram，够做透一条主路径，必须先圈定最小核心功能集。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes to design Instagram — only enough for one main path — so you first scope the minimum core feature set.

q: 哪些功能划到范围外后，就不必为它们设计专门的组件？（多选）
q_en: Which features, once scoped out, mean you no longer need to design dedicated components for them?
options: 点赞和评论
搜索用户、话题、地点
Stories（短暂内容）与直播
关注其他用户
options_en: Likes and comments
Searching users, hashtags, or locations
Stories and live streaming
Following other users
why: 点赞评论、搜索、Stories、直播都在范围外；关注是三大核心需求之一。主动列出 out-of-scope 展示产品思维，但别在上面耗时间。
why_en: Likes, comments, search, stories, and live streaming are explicitly out of scope, while following users is a core requirement.
optionExplanations: 点赞评论属于帖子发布后的互动层，产品迭代里才加，这版明确排除。
搜索用户/话题/地点是独立的发现能力，需要建索引，本版不做。
Stories 和直播各有自己的短生命周期存储和流媒体需求，独立于这版范围。
关注不算范围外——它是核心功能之一，是拉取 feed 前必须先建立的关系。
optionExplanations_en: Likes/comments are post-time engagement, added in later iterations — explicitly excluded here.
Searching users/hashtags/places is a separate discovery capability needing its own index — not in this round.
Stories and live video each need their own short-lived storage and streaming stack — out of this scope.
Following isn't out of scope — it's one of the core features and the relationship a feed must be built on.
scenario: 45 分钟的 Instagram 设计面试，划到范围外的功能就不必为它设计专门的服务与存储。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute Instagram design, anything scoped out means you do not have to design services or storage for it.

scenario: 5 亿 DAU 的照片分享应用：用户能容忍新帖晚一点出现在粉丝 feed 里，但不能容忍刷不出内容。
scenario_en: A photo-sharing app has 500M DAU. Users can tolerate a new post appearing in followers' feeds a little late, but they cannot tolerate an unavailable feed.
q: 在 CAP 权衡上应该怎么选？
q_en: For the CAP trade-off, which side should this Instagram feed design favor?
options: 强一致优先：所有新帖必须瞬间在全球所有副本上同时可见
要求可用性和强一致同时100%成立，网络分区时也拒绝二选一
可用性优先，接受最终一致（新帖最迟约 2 分钟对粉丝可见）
只对视频保证强一致，照片允许任意延迟，不做承诺
options_en: Prioritize strong consistency: every new post must be instantly visible on all global replicas.
Require both availability and strong consistency at 100%, refusing to pick either even during a network partition.
Prioritize availability, accepting eventual consistency with posts visible within about two minutes.
Guarantee strong consistency only for video; photos may lag arbitrarily with no promise.
why: 照片/视频分发对正确性容忍度高、对可用性要求高，所以选可用性优先、最终一致，并把陈旧上限量化为 2 分钟。
why_en: This system prioritizes availability over consistency, accepting eventual consistency with posts visible to followers within about two minutes.
whenOtherWins: 支付、库存、抢票这类正确性高于可用性的系统反过来：宁可暂时拒绝服务，也不能返回错误数据。
tradeoff: 可用性 + 最终一致 vs 强一致 + 全网瞬时可见

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统在网络分区时，一致性和可用性最多只能保一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can guarantee at most one of consistency or availability during a network partition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内不同副本可能不一致，但最终会收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means replicas may briefly disagree after a write but converge over time.

optionExplanations: 全球强一致需要每次写等所有副本确认，5 亿 DAU 下会拖垮发帖延迟；只有正确性压倒一切的场景才值得。
可用性和强一致在网络分区时不可能同时满足，这个选项本身就违反 CAP 定理。
接受最终一致换可用性，2 分钟的陈旧上限刚好匹配「能等但不能刷不出来」的用户预期。
只保视频强一致、照片不做承诺回避了真正的一致性决策，没有给出可执行的设计方向。
optionExplanations_en: Global strong consistency means waiting for every replica to ack on every write — at 500M DAU that blows the post latency budget; only correctness-above-all systems justify it.
Availability and strong consistency can't both fully hold during a network partition — this option contradicts CAP itself.
Trading strong consistency for availability with a 2-minute staleness cap matches users who can wait but can't tolerate a blank feed.
Guaranteeing consistency only for video while making no promise for photos dodges the real consistency decision instead of making one.

scenario: 面试官要求 feed 请求端到端有一个明确的延迟 SLA，这个数字将决定要不要做读时聚合。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks for a clear end-to-end feed latency SLA; that target decides whether read-time aggregation can work.
q: feed 请求端到端应对外承诺的响应时间边界是？
q_en: What end-to-end latency target should the feed API promise?
options: < 100ms（仅缓存命中可达）
< 500ms 端到端
< 2 秒（首屏会明显卡顿）
< 5 秒（更像后台任务）
options_en: Under 100ms (realistic only for a cache hit).
Under five hundred milliseconds end-to-end.
Under 2 seconds (visibly stalls the first screen).
Under 5 seconds (feels more like a background job).
why: feed 加载要求端到端 < 500ms，这个数字驱动了后面「预计算 feed」的深挖：读时聚合根本达不到这个目标。
why_en: The feed must be delivered with an end-to-end latency under five hundred milliseconds, which drives the precomputed-feed design.
optionExplanations: <100ms 是极低目标，通常只适合本地缓存命中，不适合作为首版端到端 SLA。
<500ms 是给定 SLA，足够倒逼预计算 feed，而不是读时逐个聚合。
<2 秒会让首页刷新明显卡顿，掩盖了读时聚合的延迟问题。
<5 秒已经像后台任务，不符合用户打开 feed 的即时体验。
optionExplanations_en: Under 100ms is an extremely tight target, usually realistic only for local cache hits, not a first-pass end-to-end SLA.
Under 500ms is the stated SLA, and it is tight enough to force a precomputed feed instead of read-time aggregation.
Under 2 seconds would make home-feed refresh feel visibly slow and hide the read-time aggregation problem.
Under 5 seconds feels more like a background job than an instant feed load.

q: 补全 Instagram 的非功能需求：
q_en: Complete Instagram's core non-functional requirements.
text: 系统{{可用性}}优先于一致性（最终一致，窗口最多 {{2 分钟}}）；feed 请求端到端 < {{500ms}}；媒体要即时渲染；规模支撑 {{5亿}} DAU。
why: 四条核心 NFR：高可用+最终一致（≤2 分钟）、feed 低延迟（<500ms）、媒体即时渲染、5 亿 DAU 可扩展。关键是找出系统独特的难点，而非罗列通用性质。
why_en: The core non-functional requirements are high availability with eventual consistency up to two minutes, feed latency under five hundred milliseconds, instant media rendering, and scale to five hundred million daily active users.

scenario: 定 NFR 之前，面试官先问清了系统规模，因为规模直接决定架构复杂度：是单机能扛，还是必须分片、缓存、异步。
scenario_en: Before setting NFRs, the interviewer clarifies scale because it determines whether a single-machine design is enough or whether sharding, caching, and async work are required.
q: 这道题要设计的目标规模是？
q_en: What target scale is this Instagram design planning for?
options: 5000 万 DAU、每天 1000 万帖
50 亿 DAU、每天 10 亿帖
100 万 DAU、每天 10 万帖
5 亿 DAU、每天 1 亿新帖
options_en: Fifty million DAU, ten million posts per day.
Five billion DAU, one billion posts per day.
One million DAU, one hundred thousand posts per day.
Five hundred million DAU, one hundred million new posts per day.
why: 规模是 500M DAU、100M posts/day。这个数字后续贯穿存储估算、fan-out 成本和缓存容量的所有推导。
why_en: The design targets five hundred million daily active users creating one hundred million posts per day.

q: 哪些属于这个设计的核心实体？（多选）
q_en: Which entities belong in the core Instagram data model?
options: User（用户资料）
Post（帖子元数据：caption、媒体引用、作者）
Media（S3 里的实际媒体字节）
Follow（follower 与 followee 的关系）
Comment（评论）
options_en: User: account profile.
Post: caption, media reference, and author metadata.
Media: the actual bytes stored in S3.
Follow: the relationship between follower and followee.
Comment: user comments on a post.
why: 四个核心实体：User、Post、Media、Follow。评论在范围外。实体阶段先给高层清单即可，schema 细节边设计边补。
why_en: The core entities are User, Post, Media, and Follow, while comments are out of scope.
optionExplanations: User 存账户资料和凭据这类身份信息，是整个系统的身份锚点。
Post 只存 caption、媒体引用和作者这些元数据，不含字节本身。
Media 是 S3 里的实际文件字节，和结构化元数据分开存储各取所长。
Follow 是有向关系，一个用户关注另一个，直接支撑 feed 生成。
Comment 是帖子下的互动层，属于后续迭代功能，这版不建为核心实体。
optionExplanations_en: User holds account profile and credential-type identity data — the identity anchor for the whole system.
Post stores only metadata — caption, media reference, author — not the media bytes themselves.
Media is the actual file bytes in S3, split from structured metadata so each store does what it's good at.
Follow is a directed relationship, one user following another, and it's what a feed is generated from.
Comment is post-time engagement layered on later — not modeled as a core entity in this round.
scenario: Instagram 设计进入实体阶段，范围只含发帖、关注、时间序 feed，实体要覆盖这三条路径。
scenario_en: Entities stage of the Instagram design: scope is posting, following, and a chronological feed, so entities must cover those three paths.

q: 关于 Post 实体的一个关键设计决定是？
q_en: What is the key design choice for the Post entity?
options: 照片和视频各建一种实体、各用一张独立的表存储，读写路径也各写一套
单一 Post 实体承载照片和视频，只存媒体引用
把媒体字节直接内嵌进 Post 记录，不使用对象存储
Post 实体只能存文字说明，完全不允许挂载媒体
options_en: Model photos and videos as two separate entities with separate tables and duplicate read/write paths.
A single Post entity handles both photos and videos, storing only a media reference.
Embed the media bytes directly inside the Post record, skipping object storage.
A Post can only hold text captions and can never attach media.
why: 一个 Post 实体统一处理照片和视频，只存媒体引用，字节放 S3。统一实体避免两套几乎一样的读写路径。
why_en: A single Post entity handles both photos and videos, holding a reference to the media file rather than the bytes themselves.
optionExplanations: 两张表意味着两套几乎重复的 schema 和查询路径，维护成本翻倍，却没有额外收益。
一个 Post 实体用 media_type 字段区分照片和视频，只存引用不存字节，读写路径统一。
把大字节内嵌进记录会把数据库表撑得又大又慢，读写吞吐都会掉。
帖子完全不能挂媒体，直接违反了「发布带照片/视频」这条核心需求。
optionExplanations_en: Two tables means two nearly-duplicate schemas and query paths, doubling maintenance for no real gain.
One Post entity with a media_type field distinguishes photo vs video, stores only a reference, and keeps one unified read/write path.
Embedding large binary bytes into the record bloats the table and drags down both read and write throughput.
A post that can never carry media directly violates the core requirement to publish photos/video.
scenario: 照片和视频的读写路径几乎相同，只有媒体类型不同；不想维护两套几乎一样的代码。
scenario_en: Photos and videos follow nearly identical read and write paths, and you do not want to maintain two near-duplicate stacks.

q: Instagram 的关注（Follow）关系有什么方向性？
q_en: What directionality does Instagram's Follow relationship have?
options: 双向：必须互相关注才能看到对方发布的帖子
双向但需要对方确认
无方向概念
单向：我关注梅西，能看他的帖子
options_en: Mutual: both users must follow each other before either can see the other’s posts.
Mutual but requires the other side's confirmation.
Following has no direction at all.
One-directional: I follow Messi and see his posts.
why: Follow 是单向关系：follower 看 followee 的帖子，反之不成立。这区别于双向好友模型，直接决定了 Follows 表按方向建索引。
why_en: Following is a one-directional relationship where the follower sees the followee's posts but not the other way around.
optionExplanations: 双向互相关注更接近好友模型，和 Instagram 的公开关注不符。
加一道确认步骤把它变成了带审批的对称关系，题目没有这个流程。
没有方向就分不清谁读谁的帖子，feed 根本生成不出来。
这是单向订阅：我能看到对方发的内容，对方看不到我发的，这个方向性正是生成 feed 要靠的关系。
optionExplanations_en: Mutual double-follow is closer to a friend model, which doesn't match Instagram's public one-way follow.
Adding an approval step turns it into a confirmed symmetric relationship — no such flow exists here.
Without direction you can't tell who reads whose posts, so a feed can't even be generated.
In a one-way relationship the follower sees the followee's posts but not vice versa — exactly the read direction a feed needs.
scenario: Follows 表要建索引支撑 feed 生成，得先确定关注关系是否对称。
scenario_en: The Follows table needs an index to drive feed generation, so first settle whether following is symmetric.

q: POST /follows 请求里为什么只有 followedId，没有 followerId？
q_en: Why does POST /follows include followedId but not followerId?
options: followerId 放在 URL 路径参数里，比如 /users/{id}/follows
系统根据请求来源 IP 自动猜测发起者身份
follower 的身份从认证凭据（JWT/session）中提取，更安全且符合最小权限原则
关注这个动作不需要记录是谁发起的，系统不追踪
options_en: The follower id goes in the URL path, such as /users/{id}/follows.
The system automatically guesses the initiator's identity from the request's source IP.
The follower's identity comes from the auth token such as a JWT or session, which is safer and follows least privilege.
Following doesn't need to record who initiated it; the system doesn't track it.
why: 发起者身份从 JWT 或 session 里取，不信任请求体，防止伪造他人身份去关注。就算写进 body，也必须和会话比对。
why_en: The follower's identity comes from the authentication token rather than the request body, which is more secure and follows least privilege.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自带签名的身份令牌，服务端可直接验证而不用查会话库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that carries identity claims, letting a server verify a user without a separate session lookup.

optionExplanations: URL 路径能放 ID，但题目给的接口是 POST /follows，body 里没有它。
凭 IP 猜身份不可靠也不安全，压根不是身份认证的做法。
身份从 JWT/session 这类凭据里提取而不是信任请求体，符合最小权限原则，防止伪造他人身份关注。
系统必须知道是谁发起了关注这个动作，否则连关系表都写不进去。
optionExplanations_en: A path param could hold the id, but this endpoint is POST /follows and the body doesn't carry it.
Guessing identity from request IP is unreliable and not how authentication works.
Identity is pulled from the JWT/session credential instead of trusting the request body — least-privilege, and it stops someone from forging another user's follow.
The system has to know who initiated the follow, or it can't even write the relationship row.
scenario: 关注接口对公网开放，任何人都能自己构造请求体，必须防止 A 冒充 B 去关注。
scenario_en: The follow endpoint is public and anyone can craft a request body, so you must stop A from impersonating B.

q: GET /feed 接口的分页设计是？
q_en: How should GET /feed handle pagination?
options: 用 page=1&size=20 这种基于页码偏移的传统分页，翻页时重算 offset
cursor + limit：返回 Post 数组和 next_cursor
不做任何分页处理，一次性把全部 feed 都返回给客户端
按用户指定的起止日期区间参数做范围查询
options_en: Traditional offset pagination like page=1&size=20, recomputing the offset on every page turn.
Cursor plus limit: return posts and a next cursor.
Skip pagination entirely and return the entire feed to the client in one response.
Query by a user-specified start and end date range parameter.
why: feed 用游标分页：GET /feed?cursor={cursor}&limit={page_size}，响应带 next_cursor。游标分页在数据不断前插的信息流里比页码稳定。
why_en: The feed endpoint uses cursor-based pagination with a limit and returns posts plus a next cursor for the following page.
optionExplanations: 页码假设列表位置稳定，但 feed 头部持续插新帖，翻页会错位或漏帖。
游标指向某条帖子，配合 limit 取下一批，新帖插入头部也不会打乱已发出的游标。
5 亿 DAU 规模下一次性吐出全部 feed，带宽和内存都扛不住。
按日期区间查适合翻旧历史，不适合持续下拉刷新的场景。
optionExplanations_en: Page numbers assume a stable list, but new posts keep landing at the top of a feed, so pages shift and posts get skipped or repeated.
A cursor points at a specific post and pairs with limit to fetch the next batch — new posts at the top don't invalidate a cursor already handed out.
Returning the entire feed in one response at 500M DAU would blow both bandwidth and memory.
A date-range query fits browsing old history, not a feed meant for continuous pull-to-refresh.
scenario: feed 顶部不断插入新帖，用户边刷边有新内容进来，分页必须不重复也不漏项。
scenario_en: New posts keep being inserted at the top of the feed while the user scrolls, so pagination must not duplicate or skip items.

q: API Gateway 在这套架构里的职责是？
q_en: What should the API Gateway do in this Instagram architecture?
options: 把客户端请求路由到对应微服务，并可承担认证、限流、日志等横切关注点
由网关直接存储和管理帖子元数据，绕开 Post Service
由网关自己负责生成用户的 feed 内容并排序返回
由网关负责媒体文件的转码、压缩和格式转换
options_en: Route client requests to the right microservice, and optionally handle auth, rate limiting, and logging.
The gateway directly stores and manages post metadata, bypassing the Post Service.
The gateway itself generates and sorts the user's feed content.
The gateway handles media transcoding, compression, and format conversion.
why: 网关是所有客户端进入系统的统一入口：核心职责是路由，同时可顺手处理认证、限流、日志这类横切逻辑，业务留给各微服务。
why_en: The API gateway routes client requests to the right microservice and can also handle cross-cutting concerns like authentication, rate limiting, and logging.
optionExplanations: 网关是统一入口，核心职责是路由，顺带能做认证、限流、日志这些横切逻辑，业务留给下游服务。
元数据持久化是 Post Service 的职责，网关自己存数据混淆了分层。
feed 生成和排序属于 Feed/Post 服务，网关不该插手业务编排。
媒体转码属于媒体处理服务，和网关的路由职责不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: The gateway is the single entry point — its core job is routing, plus cross-cutting concerns like auth, rate limiting, and logging; business logic stays downstream.
Persisting metadata belongs to the Post Service; having the gateway store data blurs the layering.
Feed generation and ranking belong to the Feed/Post service — the gateway shouldn't own business orchestration.
Media transcoding belongs to a media-processing service, not the gateway's routing job.
scenario: 移动端要访问 Post/Follow/Feed 多个微服务，不希望每个服务各自实现认证与限流。
scenario_en: Mobile clients hit the Post, Follow, and Feed services, and you do not want each one reimplementing auth and rate limiting.

q: 用户发帖时，Post Service 对「元数据」和「媒体字节」分别怎么处理？
q_en: When a user creates a post, how should Post Service handle metadata versus media bytes?
options: 把元数据和媒体字节一起写进同一条 DynamoDB 记录，靠单记录保证原子性
把结构化的元数据字段也全部写进 S3 对象存储里
元数据写 Posts DB，媒体字节写 S3，返回 postId
元数据和字节都先写进 Redis 缓存，再异步落库持久化
options_en: Write both metadata and media bytes into one DynamoDB record, relying on single-record atomicity.
Write the structured metadata fields entirely into S3 object storage too.
Write metadata to the Posts DB and media bytes to S3, returning a postId.
Write both metadata and bytes into Redis first, then flush to durable storage asynchronously.
why: 结构化元数据（作者、时间、caption、媒体链接）进数据库，字节进 S3 这类 blob store，各取所长。数据库存大二进制既贵又慢。
why_en: The post service writes structured metadata to the database and the raw media bytes to blob storage like S3, then returns a post id.
diagram:
graph LR
    Client[Client] --> Post[Post Service]
    Post --> Meta[(Metadata DB)]
    Post --> Upload[Presigned upload]
    Client --> Blob[(Object storage)]
    Blob --> Process[Media processing]
    Process --> CDN[CDN variants]

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的分布式 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed distributed NoSQL database that scales horizontally by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的对象存储服务，常用来存图片、视频等大文件字节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is AWS's object storage service, commonly used to store large binary files like images and video.

optionExplanations: 大字节写进结构化数据库会让记录体积暴涨，吞吐和成本都变差。
结构化元数据丢进对象存储会失去按字段查询的能力。
元数据进可查询的数据库，字节进 S3 这类对象存储，各自发挥所长、整体成本最优。
Redis 是缓存不是持久化主存储，重启或驱逐会丢数据。
optionExplanations_en: Writing large bytes into a structured database bloats records and hurts both throughput and cost.
Dumping structured metadata into object storage loses the ability to query by field.
Metadata goes to a queryable database, bytes go to object storage like S3 — each store does what it does best, at the lowest overall cost.
Redis is a cache, not durable primary storage — a restart or eviction can lose data.
scenario: 一条帖子含几百字节结构化字段和最大 4GB 的媒体，两者读写成本差好几个数量级。
scenario_en: A post carries a few hundred bytes of structured fields plus up to 4GB of media — costs differ by orders of magnitude.

scenario: 关注/取关的发生频率远低于发帖和刷 feed，两类流量的负载曲线完全不同。
scenario_en: Follow and unfollow happen far less often than posting and feed browsing, so the load curves are very different.
q: 为什么把 Follow 拆成独立的 Follow Service？
q_en: Why split Follow into its own service?
options: 两类操作频率和负载特征不同，拆开后可以按各自需求独立优化与扩缩容
因为两个服务绝对不能写同一个数据库
为了让 Follow 服务拆分后自动获得跨服务的强一致事务保证
因为 API Gateway 最多只能路由到两个服务
options_en: The two operations differ in frequency and load, so splitting lets each be optimized and scaled independently.
Because two services must never write to the same database.
To automatically gain cross-service strong-consistency transactions once Follow is split out.
Because the API gateway can only route to two services.
why: 拆服务的理由是负载特征不同、希望独立扩缩，而不是教条。拆与不拆是「系统复杂度 vs 运维精细度」的权衡。
why_en: Follows happen far less often than posting and viewing, so a separate follow service lets each be optimized and scaled independently.
whenOtherWins: 系统早期或规模小时，合在一个服务里更简单省事——不要为了微服务而微服务。
tradeoff: 按负载特征独立扩缩 vs 单服务简单省事
optionExplanations: 关注/取关和发帖/刷 feed 的负载曲线完全不同，拆开后才能各自按自己的流量独立扩缩容。
两个服务共享一个数据库在实践里很常见，「绝不能共享」是过度理想化的教条。
拆成两个服务反而丢了单库事务，跨服务事务需要额外的分布式事务或补偿机制才能凑出一致性，不是拆分本身送的。
网关能路由到任意数量的下游服务，数量从不是拆分的限制因素。
optionExplanations_en: Follow/unfollow and posting/reading a feed have totally different load curves — splitting them lets each scale independently to its own traffic.
Two services sharing one database is common in practice — 'never share a database' is dogma, not a real constraint.
Splitting into two services loses the single-database transaction; cross-service consistency needs extra distributed-transaction or compensation machinery — splitting doesn't hand it to you for free.
A gateway can route to any number of downstream services — count was never the limiting factor for splitting.

scenario: Post Service 和 Follow Service 需要联合读写相关数据；团队在纠结要不要给两者各建一个独立数据库。
scenario_en: Post Service and Follow Service need to read and write related data, so the team is debating one shared database versus separate databases.
q: 在「跨服务事务与引用完整性」这个维度上，共享数据库和每服务独立库谁更省事？
q_en: For cross-service transactions and referential integrity, which database ownership model is simpler?
options: 独立库在这个维度上更省事：服务边界清晰，跨库调用自带补偿机制
共享库更省事：同库内事务简单、完整性好维护
两者在这个维度上完全一样，没有区别
共享库和独立库都做不到事务保证
options_en: Separate databases are simpler here: clear service boundaries, and cross-database calls come with built-in compensation.
A shared database is simpler: single-database transactions and easy referential integrity.
The two are exactly equivalent on this dimension, no difference.
Neither shared nor separate databases can guarantee transactions.
why: 共享库的优势正是跨域事务简单、完整性好维护；代价是服务耦合更紧、互相抢性能、schema 变更要协调。
why_en: A shared database makes cross-domain transactions and referential integrity much simpler, at the cost of tighter coupling between services.
tradeoff: 事务简单 + 强完整性 vs 服务解耦 + 独立扩展
optionExplanations: 独立库把跨服务写入变成分布式事务或 Saga，反而比共享库更复杂。
同库内一次事务就能同时更新相关表，外键约束天然生效，这是共享库在这个维度上的优势。
两种方案在事务复杂度上差距很大，不是没有区别。
共享库内部完全可以用事务，只是独立库才要额外兜底最终一致。
optionExplanations_en: Separate databases turn cross-service writes into distributed transactions or a Saga — that's more complex than sharing one.
One transaction inside a shared database updates related tables together and foreign keys just work — that's the shared-database advantage on this dimension.
The two options differ a lot in transaction complexity, not equally hard.
A shared database supports transactions natively; it is the separate-database path that needs extra eventual-consistency plumbing.

q: 每个服务独立数据库要付出哪些代价？（多选）
q_en: What costs come with database-per-service?
options: 跨服务操作需要分布式事务或接受最终一致
更多数据库要维护，运维复杂度上升
基础设施成本可能更高
无法再给表建索引
options_en: Cross-service operations need distributed transactions or eventual consistency.
More databases to maintain raise operational complexity.
Infrastructure cost may be higher.
Tables can no longer have indexes.
why: 独立库换来强封装、独立扩展、可各选技术栈，但代价是分布式事务/最终一致、更重的运维、更高的成本。索引能力与是否拆库无关。
why_en: Separate databases per service bring distributed transactions or eventual consistency, more operational burden, and potentially higher infrastructure cost.
optionExplanations: 跨库写入失去了单一事务的原子性，只能靠分布式事务或接受最终一致兜底。
每个数据库都要单独备份、扩容、监控，运维要盯的面变多了。
多套实例多套备份意味着账单直接上涨。
索引是表级特性，和数据库拆不拆没有关系，这条代价不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Cross-database writes lose single-transaction atomicity — you fall back on distributed transactions or accept eventual consistency.
Each database needs its own backups, capacity, and monitoring, so ops has more surface to watch.
More instances and more backups directly means a bigger bill.
Indexing is a table-level feature unrelated to whether you split databases — this isn't a real cost.
scenario: 团队想把 Post/Follow/Feed 各拆一个独立数据库，得先把代价算清楚再决定。
scenario_en: The team wants a separate database per Post, Follow, and Feed service, so the costs must be priced out first.

q: 关于「多个服务写同一个数据库」，符合工业界现实的说法是？
q_en: What is a realistic view of multiple services writing one database?
options: 每个服务必须独占自己的数据，否则就是不可接受的反模式，必须立刻拆分
生产系统里从不存在共享数据库
必须先上分布式事务才允许共享
许多大厂生产系统就是多服务共享一库；先共享、再按需隔离
options_en: Each service must exclusively own its data, or it is an unacceptable anti-pattern that must be split immediately.
Shared databases never exist in production systems.
Distributed transactions must be in place before sharing is allowed.
Many large companies share one database across services in production; start shared and isolate later as needed.
why: 「每服务独占数据」更多是学术洁癖；Post Service 和 Follow Service 处理的是天然相关的领域概念，共享一库完全合理。多数组织从共享库起步，有需要再拆。
why_en: Many production systems at large companies have multiple services writing to one database, and starting shared then evolving toward isolation is a common, valid path.
optionExplanations: 每服务独占数据更像是学术洁癖，工业界有大量反例。
生产系统里共享库大量存在，这个说法和现实矛盾。
分布式事务昂贵复杂，不是共享库的前置条件，这个说法搞反了因果。
许多大厂就是从共享一库起步，需求变大再按需拆分，这才是常见的务实路径。
optionExplanations_en: 'Every service must own its data' is closer to academic purity than practice — there are plenty of counterexamples.
Shared databases are common in real production systems, so this claim contradicts reality.
Distributed transactions are expensive and complex, not a prerequisite for sharing a database — this gets the causality backwards.
Many large companies start with one shared database and split it only when the need actually shows up — the common, pragmatic path.
scenario: Post 与 Follow 是天然相关的领域概念，团队纠结共享一库是不是不可接受的反模式。
scenario_en: Post and Follow are naturally related domains, and the team is unsure whether sharing one database is an unacceptable anti-pattern.

q: 补全朴素 feed 生成（fan-out on read）的流程：
q_en: Complete the naive fan-out-on-read feed-generation flow.
text: 朴素做法：先查 {{Follow}} 表拿到当前用户关注的所有 userId → 对每个被关注用户查 {{Post}} 表取近期帖子 → 把所有帖子{{合并排序}}（按时间）→ 按 cursor/limit 截取返回。
why: 这就是 fan-out on read：读的时刻才去逐个聚合。小应用可行，但每次刷新都做全量聚合，是后续深挖要推翻的起点方案。
why_en: The naive fan-out-on-read feed queries the follow table, fetches recent posts per followed user, merges and sorts them chronologically, and returns a page.
diagram:
graph LR
    Request[GET /feed] --> Follow[Fetch followees]
    Follow --> Posts[Query recent posts]
    Posts --> Merge[Merge and sort]
    Merge --> Hydrate[Hydrate metadata]
    Hydrate --> Client[Return page]

scenario: 5 亿 DAU、实体间关系简单、可接受最终一致，要为帖子/关注元数据选数据库。
scenario_en: At 500M DAU with simple relationships and acceptable eventual consistency, choose a database for post and follow metadata.
q: 该给帖子和关注元数据选哪种数据库？
q_en: Which database should store post and follow metadata?
options: 单机 MySQL：关系模型最成熟、生态最完善
DynamoDB：水平扩展强、按 key 访问、可接受最终一致
Neo4j 图数据库：关注关系天生适合图查询，多跳遍历性能最好
全内存 HashMap：读写延迟最低最快
options_en: Single-node MySQL: the most mature relational model with the richest ecosystem.
DynamoDB: horizontal scale, key-based access, eventual consistency is fine.
Neo4j: follow relationships are naturally graph-shaped, with the best multi-hop traversal performance.
An all in-memory HashMap: the lowest possible read and write latency.
why: 规模大、关系少、容忍最终一致，指向 DynamoDB 这类可水平扩展的 NoSQL。但这不是唯一正解，关键是能为自己的选型给出理由。
why_en: Given the scale, few relationships, and acceptable eventual consistency, DynamoDB is chosen, though PostgreSQL would be equally defensible.
whenOtherWins: PostgreSQL 等关系库同样成立——Instagram 生产就用 Postgres 存帖子元数据；选它就从索引与分片角度自圆其说。
tradeoff: 水平扩展 + 最终一致 vs 关系模型成熟度

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的分布式 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed distributed NoSQL database that scales horizontally by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门优化多跳图遍历查询的图数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Neo4j is a graph database optimized for multi-hop traversal queries.

optionExplanations: 单机 MySQL 生态最成熟，但要撑千倍增长得额外做复制分片，工程量不小。
DynamoDB 按 key 访问模式水平扩展，5 亿 DAU、关系简单、能容忍最终一致时正好对上。
图数据库擅长多跳遍历，但单向关注只需要简单读写，用不上这层能力。
全内存结构没有持久化和跨机分布能力，规模一大直接不可行。
optionExplanations_en: Single-node MySQL has the most mature ecosystem, but scaling it a thousandfold needs extra replication and sharding work.
DynamoDB scales horizontally by key access pattern — a good fit when you have 500M DAU, simple relationships, and can tolerate eventual consistency.
Graph databases shine at multi-hop traversal, but a one-way follow only needs simple reads/writes, so that strength goes unused.
An in-memory structure has no durability or cross-machine distribution, so it is a non-starter at this scale.

scenario: 团队担心 NoSQL 是不是唯一能撑住 5 亿 DAU 的路线，想找一个真实案例检验这个假设。
scenario_en: The team worries NoSQL may be the only path to 500M DAU and wants a real-world case to test that belief.
q: Instagram 生产环境用 PostgreSQL 撑起 5 亿 DAU 这一事实，说明了什么？
q_en: What does Instagram running PostgreSQL at 500M DAU prove?
options: 说明 SQL 也能扩展到超大规模，「SQL 扛不了大规模」是过时论调
说明 Instagram 的真实用户规模其实一直很小，公开的 DAU 数字被夸大了
说明 NoSQL 数据库在架构设计上存在根本性的缺陷
说明关系模型天生就不适合高并发的社交类产品
options_en: It shows SQL can scale to massive size; "SQL can’t scale" is outdated.
It shows Instagram’s real user base has always been small and the public DAU figure is inflated.
It shows NoSQL databases have a fundamental architectural flaw.
It shows relational models are inherently unsuited to high-concurrency social products.
why: Instagram 主帖子元数据库是 PostgreSQL，证明 SQL 数据库照样能撑 5 亿 DAU，为选型面试里的 SQL 方案提供真实依据。
why_en: Instagram actually runs PostgreSQL as its main post metadata store, proving SQL databases can scale to five hundred million daily users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 成熟的开源关系型数据库，支持事务和丰富索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is a mature open-source relational database with transactions and rich indexing.

optionExplanations: Instagram 生产用 PostgreSQL 撑住 5 亿 DAU，直接反驳了「SQL 扛不住大规模」这个过时论调。
案例讲的是数据库选型，和用户规模大小无关，这个推论跑偏了。
案例证明的是 SQL 可行，不代表 NoSQL 有架构缺陷，两者不是对立面。
案例的结论恰恰相反：关系模型证明了自己能扛住社交规模的高并发。
optionExplanations_en: Instagram runs 500M DAU on production PostgreSQL — that directly refutes the outdated claim that SQL can't handle large scale.
The case is about database choice, not about how big Instagram's user base actually is — that inference misses the point.
The case proves SQL is viable; it says nothing about NoSQL being architecturally flawed — they aren't opposites.
The conclusion runs the other way: the relational model just proved it can handle social-scale concurrency.

scenario: DynamoDB 里建 Follows 表，最高频查询是「取某用户关注的所有人」（读 feed 的第一步），必须避免全表扫描。
scenario_en: In a DynamoDB Follows table, the hottest query is getting everyone a user follows, so full table scans must be avoided.
q: Follows 表主键应该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the DynamoDB Follows table primary key be designed?
options: 分区键 followedId、排序键 followerId
只有分区键 followerId，不设排序键
分区键 postId、排序键 createdAt
分区键 followerId、排序键 followedId
options_en: Partition key followedId, sort key followerId.
Only a partition key followerId, no sort key.
Partition key postId, sort key createdAt.
Partition key followerId, sort key followedId.
why: 按 followerId 分区，一次 Query 就能拿到该用户关注的全部人；followedId 做排序键保证行唯一。键设计永远跟着主访问模式走。
why_en: Partitioning by follower id with followed id as the sort key lets one query return everyone a given user follows.
whenOtherWins: 反向问题「谁关注了我」要靠 GSI（followedId 作分区键、followerId 作排序键），发帖 fan-out 时用的正是那条索引。
tradeoff: 按 followerId 分区服务「我关注了谁」vs 按 followedId 分区服务「谁关注了我」

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引，允许用不同的分区键/排序键从另一个方向查询同一张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI, or global secondary index, lets you query the same table by a different partition and sort key.

optionExplanations: 分区方向反了，这个键服务的是「谁关注了我」，不是本题要的查询。
缺排序键就没法在一个分区内唯一标识每一行，也没法分页。
postId 和 createdAt 是帖子表的维度，跟关注关系完全不是一回事。
分区键用 followerId 直接对准「取某人关注了谁」这条主查询，排序键 followedId 保证行唯一。
optionExplanations_en: This partitions the wrong way — it serves 'who follows me,' not the query this card actually needs.
Without a sort key you can't uniquely identify each row within a partition or paginate it.
postId and createdAt are Post-table dimensions, unrelated to a follow relationship.
Partitioning on followerId maps directly to the main query 'who does this user follow,' and followedId as sort key keeps rows unique.

scenario: Posts 表最高频查询是「取某个用户的帖子并按时间倒序」，同一用户同一时刻可能发多帖，主键还必须唯一。
scenario_en: The hottest Posts-table query fetches one user's posts in reverse time order, and multiple posts may share the same timestamp.
q: Posts 表主键应该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the DynamoDB Posts table primary key be designed?
options: 分区键 userId、排序键 createdAt#postId 复合键
只有分区键 postId
分区键 createdAt、排序键 userId，按时间天然全局有序
分区键 caption、排序键 userId
options_en: Partition key userId, sort key a composite of createdAt and postId.
Only a partition key postId.
Partition key createdAt with sort key userId, giving natural global time ordering.
Partition key caption, sort key userId.
why: 按 userId 分区匹配「查某人的帖子」；排序键用 createdAt 和 postId 的复合，既保证时间序又保证唯一。
why_en: Partitioning posts by user id with a composite sort key of created time and post id gives chronological order plus uniqueness.
whenOtherWins: 如果主访问模式是单帖详情页（按 postId 直查），单键 postId 的表或 GSI 更合适；这里主流量是拉某人的时间线。
codeSample:
// DynamoDB Posts 表
KeySchema:
  partitionKey: userId
  sortKey:      createdAt#postId  // 时间序 + 唯一性

// 某用户最新 10 帖（倒序）
Query(Posts, userId = "leomessi",
      ScanIndexForward = false, Limit = 10)
tradeoff: 按 userId 分区服务「拉某人时间线」vs 按 postId 分区服务「单帖详情查询」
optionExplanations: 分区键 userId 对准「查某人的帖子」，createdAt#postId 复合排序键既保时序又保唯一。
只按 postId 分区服务的是单帖详情查询，不是本题「拉某用户时间线」这条主流程。
拿时间戳做分区键会让同一时刻的新帖全挤进一个分区，形成写热点。
caption 是自由文本，完全不该承担分区维度这个角色。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning on userId matches 'fetch a user's posts,' and the composite sort key createdAt#postId keeps chronological order while staying unique.
Partitioning only by postId serves single-post lookups, not the main 'pull one user's timeline' flow.
Using a timestamp as the partition key crams every post from the same moment into one partition — a write hotspot.
Caption is free text; it has no business acting as a partition dimension.

scenario: Instagram feed 采用 fan-out on read：用户每次打开 feed，服务临时去读取所有关注账号的近期帖子，再合并排序。这个用户关注了 1000+ 个账号。
scenario_en: The Instagram feed uses fan-out on read: on every feed open, the service reads recent posts from all followed accounts and merges them. This user follows 1000+ accounts.
q: 在这种读时聚合方案里，刷新一次 feed 会怎样压到 Posts 表？
q_en: In fan-out on read, how does one feed refresh pressure the Posts table?
options: 只要提前给 Posts 表建好按作者+时间的复合索引，一次范围查询就能取回全部关注者的帖子
无论用户关注多少人，固定只需要发出 10 次查询
每个被关注者一次查询，共 1000+ 次；即便用批量 API 也要至少 10 批
0 次数据库查询，全部命中缓存完全不用回源查询
options_en: With a composite author-plus-time index built ahead of time, one range query returns all followees’ posts.
Regardless of how many people a user follows, always exactly ten queries.
One query per followed account, over a thousand total; batch APIs still need at least ten rounds.
Zero database queries, since everything hits cache with absolutely no origin fetch needed.
why: fan-out on read 的成本跟关注数一起增长；即使用批量 API，也只是把 1000 次请求打包成多批，没有消除按关注数放大的工作量。
why_en: Fan-out on read scales with the number of followed accounts; batching reduces round trips but does not remove the follower-count-sized aggregation work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读请求到来时才把多个来源的数据拉取、合并、排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A design where the system fetches, merges, and ranks data from many sources at read time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个小请求打包成少数几个请求，减少网络往返，但通常不减少总数据处理量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API that groups many small requests into fewer calls; it reduces round trips but not necessarily total work.

optionExplanations: 索引只加速单次查询，不会把 1000 个作者的读取合成一次。
把成本当成和关注数无关的常数，忽略了它其实随关注数线性放大。
每个被关注者一次查询，1000+ 关注就要 1000+ 次，批量 API 最多把它压成十几批，量级没变。
假设全部命中缓存，忽略了缓存未命中时仍要回退到读时聚合。
optionExplanations_en: An index only speeds up a single query — it can't turn 1000 authors' reads into one.
Treating the cost as a constant regardless of follow count ignores that it actually scales linearly with it.
1000+ follows means 1000+ per-author queries; batching only packs it into roughly a dozen calls — the volume does not change.
Assuming everything hits cache ignores that a cache miss still falls back to the expensive read-time aggregation.

scenario: 用户关注了 1000 个账号，feed 服务要用 DynamoDB 的批量接口去读取这些账号的近期帖子。
scenario_en: A user follows 1000 accounts, and the feed service wants to use DynamoDB batch reads to fetch recent posts from those accounts.
q: DynamoDB 批量操作单批容量的硬上限是？
q_en: What is the hard per-batch limit for DynamoDB batch operations?
options: 25 items / 4MB
100 items / 16MB
1000 items / 64MB
没有限制
options_en: Twenty-five items or four megabytes.
One hundred items or sixteen megabytes.
One thousand items or sixty-four megabytes.
No limit at all.
why: 每批最多 100 items、16MB。所以关注 1000 个账号至少要 10 个批量操作——就算并行，也改变不了读放大的本质。
why_en: DynamoDB batch operations are limited to one hundred items and sixteen megabytes per batch, so a thousand followed accounts need at least ten batches.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的分布式 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed distributed NoSQL database.

q: fan-out on read 在 Instagram 规模下的三大问题是？（多选）
q_en: What are the three main problems with fan-out on read at Instagram scale?
options: 读放大：5 亿 DAU 每天刷多次，数据库读量爆炸、成本失控
重复劳动：大家共同关注的热门帖被反复查询上百万次
性能不可预测：延迟取决于关注了多少人、这些人多活跃
写放大：每次发帖要写数百万粉丝的 feed
options_en: Read amplification: 500M DAU refreshing repeatedly explodes database reads and cost.
Repeated work: a popular post shared by many followers gets queried millions of times over.
Unpredictable performance: latency depends on follow count and how active those accounts are.
Write amplification: each post writes to millions of followers' feeds.
why: 读放大、重复劳动、不可预测延迟是 fan-out on read 的三宗罪。写放大恰恰相反——那是 fan-out on write 的问题。
why_en: Fan-out on read suffers read amplification, repeated work for shared popular posts, and unpredictable latency, whereas write amplification belongs to fan-out on write.
optionExplanations: 读操作次数随关注数线性增长，5 亿 DAU 天天刷会把数据库读量和账单一起推爆。
大家共同关注的热门帖被反复独立查询上百万次，完全没有复用。
延迟取决于这个用户关注了多少人、这些人多活跃，同一用户不同时刻体验也不稳定。
写放大方向反了——那是写时预计算方案的代价，不是读时聚合的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Read count scales linearly with follow count — at 500M DAU refreshing daily, database read volume and cost both blow up.
A post everyone commonly follows gets queried independently millions of times with zero reuse.
Latency depends on how many accounts a user follows and how active they are, so even the same user's experience varies visit to visit.
Write amplification points the wrong way — that is the cost of precomputing on write, not a read-time aggregation problem.
scenario: 5 亿 DAU 每天多次刷 feed，而 feed 是读时才去聚合所关注账号的近期帖子。
scenario_en: With 500M DAU refreshing many times a day, the feed is aggregated from followed accounts only at read time.

scenario: 5 亿 DAU，人均单日刷新 5 次 feed，团队要用这个数字估算数据库要扛住的总负载。
scenario_en: With 500M DAU and five feed refreshes per user per day, the team uses this number to estimate total database load.
q: 5 亿用户单日合计的 feed 生成次数应归到哪个区间？
q_en: What bucket does the daily number of feed generations fall into?
options: 5 亿次
100 亿次
25 亿次
options_en: Five hundred million times.
Ten billion times.
Fifty million times.
Two and a half billion times.
why: 500M × 5 = 25 亿次/天。这组数字一摆出来，读时聚合方案就站不住了，因为每次还要处理上万条候选帖。
why_en: Five hundred million users refreshing five times daily means about two and a half billion feed generations per day.

scenario: 全天 25 亿次 feed 生成并非均匀分布，晚高峰或重大事件期间会出现明显的流量尖峰，团队要为峰值容量做规划。
scenario_en: The 2.5B daily feed generations are not evenly spread; evening peaks and major events drive much higher capacity needs.
q: 晚高峰或大事件期间，feed 请求的峰值速率应按哪个区间规划容量？
q_en: What peak feed-request rate should capacity planning assume during spikes?
options: 15 万+ 每秒
150 每秒
1500 万每秒
options_en: Over one hundred fifty thousand per second.
Fifteen hundred per second.
One hundred fifty per second.
Fifteen million per second.
why: 峰值约 150,000+ feed 请求/秒。要么疯狂超配数据库贵到离谱，要么接受高峰超时违反 500ms——所以必须换架构而不是堆容量。
why_en: Peak load reaches over one hundred fifty thousand feed requests per second, which brute-force database capacity cannot economically absorb.

scenario: Instagram 首页 feed 的朴素方案是：用户打开 feed 时，服务才去读取所有关注账号的近期帖子，再合并排序、分页返回。一个重度用户可能关注 1000+ 个账号。
scenario_en: The naive Instagram home feed reads every followed account's recent posts at request time, merges them, and pages the result. A heavy user may follow 1000+ accounts.
q: 从系统设计角度看，fan-out on read 的根本缺陷是什么？
q_en: What is the root system-design flaw in fan-out on read?
options: 底层数据库单次点查太慢，换成 DynamoDB 就能根治
把计算推迟到读取时刻——恰好是用户最期待立即响应的时候
图片/CDN 下载占满网络带宽，所以 feed API 变慢
缺少按时间排序的索引，给 Posts 表加索引就能根治
options_en: Single-row lookups are too slow; switching to DynamoDB would fix it.
Work is deferred to read time, exactly when users expect an instant response.
Image and CDN downloads saturate bandwidth, so the feed API slows down.
There's no chronological index; adding one to Posts would fix it.
why: 根因不是 DynamoDB 慢，也不是某个索引没建好；即使用很快的 NoSQL，重度用户每次刷新仍要按关注数拉取、合并、排序。
why_en: Fan-out on read is not mainly a DynamoDB or indexing problem; the flaw is doing follower-scale aggregation on the latency-sensitive read path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读请求到来时才把很多来源展开查询、合并、排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feed strategy that gathers and merges many sources at read time.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的分布式 NoSQL/键值文档数据库；是否适合取决于访问模式和分区设计，不等于天然慢或天然万能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS managed distributed NoSQL storage; suitability depends on access patterns and partition design, not a blanket slow-or-fast label.

optionExplanations: DynamoDB 本身可以很快也能水平扩展，问题根本不在数据库选型。
根因是把聚合工作留到了读的那一刻——恰好是用户最期待立即响应的时候。
这里讨论的是跨作者合并的问题，不是媒体下载占带宽的问题。
索引能帮单作者查询，但消不掉跨上千作者做合并排序这份读时工作。
optionExplanations_en: DynamoDB itself can be fast and scale horizontally — the database choice was never the real problem.
The root cause is doing the aggregation work at read time — exactly the moment the user is waiting for an instant response.
This is about merging across authors, not about media downloads eating bandwidth.
An index helps a single-author query but cannot remove the read-time work of merging and sorting across a thousand authors.

scenario: 用户每天浏览数百条帖子，却只偶尔发一条——读写比极端悬殊。
scenario_en: Users browse hundreds of posts per day but create posts only occasionally, so reads massively outnumber writes.
q: 这对应哪个通用模式、有哪些配套手段？
q_en: Which common pattern fits Instagram's extreme read-heavy workload?
options: 写扩展：靠 LSM 树结构与批量写入来提升写吞吐
长任务管理：用消息队列加后台 worker 异步处理耗时任务，接口先返回
读扩展：按 userId 分片、按数据类型垂直分区、老内容分层存储
大文件（large blobs）模式：分块上传超大文件
options_en: Scaling writes: LSM tree structures and batched writes to raise write throughput.
Managing long tasks: a message queue and background workers handle slow jobs while the API returns immediately.
Scaling reads: shard by userId, vertically partition by data type, tier old content.
The large-blobs pattern: chunked upload of oversized files.
why: Instagram 是教科书级的读扩展场景：极端读写比要求按 userId 分片、资料/帖子/分析数据垂直分区、老内容下沉冷存储。
why_en: Instagram is a textbook scaling-reads scenario, calling for sharding posts by user id, vertical partitioning by data type, and hierarchical storage for old content.
whenOtherWins: 遥测、日志摄取这类写远大于读的系统，优先套写扩展模式而不是读扩展。
tradeoff: 读扩展手段 vs 写扩展手段
optionExplanations: LSM 树和批量写提升的是写吞吐，这里的瓶颈方向根本不是写。
队列+worker 解决的是耗时任务异步化，不针对读写比失衡这个问题。
读多写少的极端比例，标准打法是按 userId 分片、按数据类型垂直分区、老内容分层存储。
大文件模式针对的是超大媒体的分块传输，不是读写比失衡。
optionExplanations_en: LSM trees and batched writes boost write throughput — the bottleneck here isn't on the write side at all.
A queue plus workers async-izes long tasks — it does not address a lopsided read/write ratio.
For an extreme read-heavy ratio, the standard playbook is shard by userId, partition by data type, and tier old content into colder storage.
The large-blob pattern is for chunking huge media transfers, not for a skewed read/write ratio.

scenario: 先不动架构，用最小改动缓解 fan-out on read：在 Posts 表前面加一层 Redis，缓存每个用户的 feed 页。
scenario_en: As the smallest change to relieve fan-out on read, the team adds Redis in front of the Posts table and caches each user's feed pages.
q: 缓存 key 的合理设计是？
q_en: What is a reasonable Redis cache key for cached feed pages?
options: 用 feed:{postId} 作为缓存 key
feed:{user_id}:{cursor}，值为该页 postId 列表
所有用户共用一个全局 key：feed:all
用 feed:{followedId} 作为缓存 key，按被关注者维度聚合缓存
options_en: Use feed:{postId} as the cache key.
feed:{user_id}:{cursor}, holding that page’s list of post ids.
All users share one single global key: feed:all.
Use feed:{followedId} as the cache key, aggregating the cache by followed author.
why: 按用户+游标组合作 key，正好对应「某用户 feed 的某一页」；命中直接返回，未命中查库后回填。
why_en: Keying the cache by user id plus cursor stores one page of that user's feed as a list of post ids.
whenOtherWins: 一旦升级到预计算 feed，key 就变成 feed:{user_id} 的 ZSET，用 score 范围分页，而不是按 cursor 切成多个 key。
tradeoff: 按用户+游标隔离分页 vs 全局共享一个 key
optionExplanations: 按帖子 ID 缓存没有隔离不同用户，谁的 feed 都会互相串。
key 里同时带用户和游标两个维度，同一用户翻到第几页都能被精确命中或按需回填，不会互相覆盖。
所有人共用一个 key 等于所有人看同一份 feed，完全违背个性化的需求。
维度选反了——应该按发起请求的用户分，而不是按被关注者分。
optionExplanations_en: Keying by post id does not isolate different users' feeds — everyone's feed would bleed into everyone else's.
Combining user id and cursor into the key matches exactly 'this user's page N' — a hit returns directly, a miss refills from the database.
One global key for everyone means everyone sees the same feed — that breaks personalization entirely.
This picks the wrong dimension — it should key on the requesting user, not on who they follow.

scenario: 团队发现 feed 读时聚合太慢，于是提出「把 feed 结果缓存起来」。但用户关注关系、帖子更新和热门事件都在持续变化。
scenario_en: The team proposes caching feed results after discovering read-time aggregation is too slow, but follows, posts, and hot events keep changing.
q: 为什么只加缓存通常只能缓解 fan-out on read，而不能根治？
q_en: Why does adding a cache only mitigate fan-out on read instead of fixing it?
options: 缓存能缓解命中请求，但未命中仍要做昂贵聚合，只是治标不治本
Redis 底层的数据结构根本不支持存储列表类型的数据
加缓存这个动作本身会直接引起严重的写放大问题
缓存条目根本无法设置任何形式的过期时间
options_en: Cache helps hits, but misses still run the expensive aggregation, treating symptoms not the cause.
Redis's underlying data structures fundamentally don't support storing list-type data.
Adding a cache directly and inherently causes serious write amplification.
Cache entries cannot have any form of expiration time set at all.
why: 缓存只改变命中请求：命中直接返回，未命中、过期或关注关系变更后仍要临时拉关注者帖子并排序。真正降读放大，要把大部分工作搬到写时预计算，或用名人读时合并的混合方案。
why_en: A cache only speeds up hits; misses, expirations, and follow changes still do read-time aggregation, so the real fix is precompute or a hybrid feed.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是短期止血、feed 页重复访问高且允许短暂旧数据，先加 TTL 缓存很划算；流量继续放大时再迁到预计算或混合方案。
tradeoff: 命中缓存省读延迟 vs 失效后仍读时聚合

termDefinitions.meaning: 读时扇出：每次读 feed 时临时读取所有关注对象的近期帖子，再合并排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read means building the feed at request time by fetching followed authors' recent posts and merging them.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 是常用的内存数据存储，常拿来做缓存、队列或有序集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory data store commonly used for caches, queues, and sorted sets.

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL 是缓存条目的存活时间，到期后条目会失效并需要重新生成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time a cached entry stays valid before it expires and must be rebuilt.

optionExplanations: 这个选项就是本题核心：缓存只兜住重复读，条目过期、被挤出或用户关系变化时仍回到读时聚合。
Redis 支持 List 和 Sorted Set，feed 页或预计算 feed 都能存在里面；问题不是容器，而是失效和未命中。
写放大来自 fan-out on write 预写粉丝 feed；只缓存读结果主要增加内存和失效管理成本。
缓存可以设置 TTL，也可以主动失效；难点是过期后仍要重算，以及新关注或新帖何时可见。
optionExplanations_en: This is the core issue: a cache covers repeated reads, but eviction, expiry, or relationship changes fall back to read-time aggregation.
Redis supports Lists and Sorted Sets; the hard part is not storage shape, but misses and invalidation.
Write amplification comes from fan-out-on-write precompute; a read cache mainly adds memory use and invalidation work.
Caches can use TTLs or active invalidation; the problem is the recompute after expiry and freshness after new events.

scenario: 读写比极端（天天刷、偶尔发），feed 必须 <500ms，读时聚合已被数字证明不可行。
scenario_en: The workload is extremely read-heavy, feed reads must stay under 500ms, and the math has ruled out read-time aggregation.
q: 更根本的解法是？
q_en: What is the more fundamental fix for slow feed reads?
options: 升级到更贵的大规格数据库实例，用更强算力硬扛全部聚合查询流量
让客户端在本地拉取数据并自行拼装完整的 feed
每次请求都并行发出 1000 个独立的数据库查询
fan-out on write：写时预计算进粉丝 feed
options_en: Upgrade to a bigger, pricier database instance and use more raw compute to brute-force every aggregation query.
Let the client fetch data locally and assemble the entire feed itself on-device.
Issue one thousand independent parallel database queries on every single request.
Fan-out on write: precompute into follower feeds at write time.
why: 把工作从读时挪到写时：发帖那一刻更新所有粉丝的预计算 feed，读就变成一次极快的 Redis 查询。读多写少的系统里，这笔交换很划算。
why_en: Fan-out on write precomputes each follower's feed at posting time, turning a feed read into a single fast Redis lookup.
whenOtherWins: 百万粉名人的写放大不可承受，所以名人帖仍走读时合并——最终落点是混合方案，而非纯 fan-out on write。
tradeoff: 预计算换快读 vs 读时聚合换简单写
optionExplanations: 堆更贵的机型只提升单点吞吐，改变不了按关注数聚合的本质，很快又会撞新上限。
把拼装工作转给客户端，网络流量和客户端逻辑复杂度都会飙升。
并行发 1000 个查询只是把总耗时压缩了，请求数和数据库负载并没有减少。
把聚合工作从读时搬到写时，发帖那一刻算好，读路径就变成一次快查——读多写少时这笔交换很划算。
optionExplanations_en: A bigger, pricier instance only raises single-node throughput; it doesn't change the per-follow-count aggregation, and you'll hit a new ceiling soon.
Pushing the assembly work to the client spikes both network traffic and client-side complexity.
Firing 1000 queries in parallel only compresses total latency — the request count and database load do not actually drop.
Moving the aggregation from read time to write time means it is done once at post time, so reading becomes one fast lookup — a great trade when reads vastly outnumber writes.

scenario: 发帖后 fan-out 服务要立刻找到「谁在关注发帖人」；但 Follows 主表按 followerId 分区，方向反了。
scenario_en: After a post is created, the fan-out service must quickly find the author's followers, but the main Follows table is partitioned by followerId.
q: 需要补什么索引？
q_en: Which index is needed to fan out a new post to followers?
options: 什么索引都不用加，主表原样就能查
对 caption 字段建一个本地二级索引（LSI），靠文本匹配反查粉丝
GSI：followedId 分区键、followerId 排序键
直接对 Follows 表做一次全表扫描
options_en: No index needed at all; the main table already supports this query as-is.
Build a local secondary index (LSI) on the caption field and find followers by text matching.
A GSI with followedId as the partition key and followerId as the sort key.
Just run a full table scan on the Follows table directly.
why: fan-out 要按「被关注者」反查粉丝列表，所以建 GSI 把方向倒过来：followedId 分区、followerId 排序，一次 Query 拿到全部粉丝。
why_en: A global secondary index with followed id as the partition key and follower id as the sort key lets the fan-out service quickly find all followers of the poster.
whenOtherWins: 「我关注了谁」由主表（followerId 分区）负责；两个查询方向各自养一条索引，谁也替代不了谁。
tradeoff: 主表服务「我关注了谁」vs GSI 服务「谁关注了我」
optionExplanations: 主表按 followerId 分区，方向反了，查不出「谁在关注这个人」。
本地二级索引只能作用于同分区内字段，caption 也和这条查询完全无关。
建 GSI 把方向倒过来，followedId 做分区键、followerId 做排序键，一次 Query 就能拿到全部粉丝。
全表扫描在这个规模下代价高到不可接受，每次发帖都扫一遍撑不住。
optionExplanations_en: The main table partitions by followerId — the wrong direction to find 'who follows this person.'
A local secondary index only works within the same partition, and caption has nothing to do with this query anyway.
A GSI flips the direction: partition on followedId, sort on followerId, so one Query returns the poster's entire follower list.
A full table scan is unaffordable at this scale — doing it on every single post would never keep up.

scenario: 每个用户的预计算 feed 要支持：新帖插入、按时间倒序取前 N 条、并能截断控制长度。
scenario_en: Each precomputed user feed must support inserting new posts, reading the newest N in reverse time order, and trimming length.
q: 读下面的 Redis 命令，正确的结构选择是？
q_en: What Redis structure do these commands point to?
options: Sorted Set：ZADD 按时间戳 score 插入，ZREVRANGE 取最新 N 条
List：用 LPUSH 插入、LRANGE 取范围，靠插入顺序保证时间序，无需 score
String：把整个 feed 序列化成一个巨大的 JSON 字符串存储
Pub/Sub：用 SUBSCRIBE 订阅一个 feed 消息频道
options_en: A sorted set: ZADD with the timestamp as score, ZREVRANGE for the newest N.
List: LPUSH to insert and LRANGE to read a range, relying on insertion order for time sequence with no score.
String: serialize the entire feed into one giant JSON string for storage.
Pub/Sub: use SUBSCRIBE to listen on a feed message channel.
why: ZSET 以时间戳为 score，天然按时间排序、成员去重，取 top N 是一次 O(logN) 范围操作——正是 feed 需要的读写形态。
why_en: A Redis sorted set with timestamps as scores keeps each feed chronologically ordered and lets the top posts be read in one fast operation.
whenOtherWins: 只需要严格插入序、不需要去重和范围查时，List 更省内存。
codeSample:
ZADD feed:u123 1718000000 post:987   # 加成员 post:987，score=时间戳；已存在则更新
ZREVRANGE feed:u123 0 19             # 按 score 降序(REV)取排名[0,19]=最新 20 条
ZREMRANGEBYRANK feed:u123 0 -801     # 按排名删：留最新 800 条(-801=倒数第801，其余删)
# 对比：ZRANGE=升序(最旧在前)，ZREVRANGE=降序(最新在前)；feed 用 REV
tradeoff: ZSET 原生排序去重 vs List 更省内存
optionExplanations: ZADD 用时间戳做 score 插入，ZREVRANGE 按时间倒序取前 N 条，排序、去重、截断三件事一次搞定。
List 保留插入序但没有排序和去重语义，score 字段用不上。
整个 feed 序列化成一个大 JSON 字符串，会丧失单条增删和范围查询的能力。
Pub/Sub 只做消息订阅通知，不能持久化存储 feed 数据。
optionExplanations_en: ZADD inserts with the timestamp as score, ZREVRANGE pulls the newest N in one range op — sorting, de-duping, and trimming all in one structure.
A List preserves insertion order but has no sort or de-dup semantics — the score field would go unused.
Serializing the whole feed into one giant JSON string loses the ability to add/remove single entries or range-query.
Pub/Sub only does message notification — it cannot persist feed data at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的一种类型:每个 member(唯一字符串)绑一个 score(浮点)，Redis 自动按 score 排序。=集合(成员唯一去重)+排序分。feed 用法:member=postId、score=时间戳，帖子就自动按时间排好。插入/取范围都是 O(logN)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis type where each member (unique string) has a score (float) and Redis keeps members sorted by score. = a set (unique members) + an ordering score. Feed usage: member=postId, score=timestamp, so posts stay time-ordered. Insert/range are O(logN).

termDefinitions.meaning: ZADD key score member：往有序集合加一个成员并给它 score;成员已存在就更新 score。发帖=ZADD feed:uX <时间戳> postId，新帖时间戳大、落在高分端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZADD key score member: add a member with a score to a sorted set; if it already exists, update its score. Posting = ZADD feed:uX <timestamp> postId; newer posts get bigger timestamps at the high-score end.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZRANGE key start stop=按 score 升序(最旧在前)取排名区间;ZREVRANGE=降序(REV=reverse，最新在前)。排名 0 基、含两端，所以 0..N-1 = top N。feed 要最新在前→用 ZREVRANGE feed:uX 0 19 取最新 20 条。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZRANGE key start stop returns a rank range in ascending score order (oldest first); ZREVRANGE is descending (REV=reverse, newest first). Ranks are 0-based inclusive, so 0..N-1 = top N. A feed wants newest-first → ZREVRANGE feed:uX 0 19 for the newest 20.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按「排名」删成员来截断 feed。排名升序(0=最低分=最旧)，负下标从末尾数(-1=最高排名=最新)。ZREMRANGEBYRANK feed:uX 0 -801 = 删排名[0,倒数第801]、只留最新 800 条。这样每次插帖后截一刀，feed 长度可控。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZREMRANGEBYRANK trims a feed by removing members in a rank range. Ranks ascend (0=lowest score=oldest); negative indices count from the end (-1=highest rank=newest). ZREMRANGEBYRANK feed:uX 0 -801 removes ranks [0, 801st-from-end], keeping the newest 800. Trimming after each insert bounds the feed length.

termDefinitions.meaning: List(LPUSH/LRANGE)按插入顺序、可重复;ZSET 成员唯一(去重)、按 score(时间)排、O(logN) 取 top-N 与按 rank 截断。feed 要「去重+按时间+取最新N+截断」，ZSET 全中，所以选它不选 List。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A List (LPUSH/LRANGE) orders by insertion and allows duplicates; a ZSET has unique members (dedup), orders by score (time), and does O(logN) top-N and rank-trim. A feed needs dedup + time order + newest-N + trim, all of which ZSET provides — hence ZSET over List.

why: feed 只存轻量的 postId 而不是完整帖子，靠 score 保证时间序；完整元数据在读取时再「水合」出来。
why_en: Each precomputed feed is a Redis sorted set whose members are post ids and whose scores are timestamps.

rows: 保留固定窗口最新数据

scenario: 团队在对比两种 feed 生成时机：fan-out on read（读时聚合）与 fan-out on write（写时预计算），要说清楚工作到底发生在哪一刻。
scenario_en: The team is comparing fan-out on read and fan-out on write and needs to explain exactly when the aggregation work happens.
q: fan-out on read 与 fan-out on write 的本质区别（工作发生在何时）是？
q_en: When does fan-out on read do the work compared with fan-out on write?
options: 两种策略的聚合工作全部都发生在读请求到达的那一刻，写入路径完全一致
on read 读时聚合；on write 写时预计算，读只剩一次查询
两种策略的聚合工作全部都发生在用户发帖写入的那一刻
两者的区别只是底层用的数据库品牌不一样而已，其他都相同
options_en: Both strategies do all aggregation the moment a read arrives, with identical write paths.
On read aggregates at read time; on write precomputes at write time, leaving one lookup.
Both strategies do all their aggregation work at the exact moment a post is written.
The only difference between the two is the underlying database brand; everything else is identical.
why: 一个是「读时现算」，一个是「写时备好」。读多写少时把成本移到写侧收益巨大——这正是选择 on write 的核心逻辑。
why_en: Fan-out on read pays the aggregation cost at read time while fan-out on write shifts it to posting time, leaving reads as one cheap lookup.
tradeoff: 读时现算 vs 写时备好
optionExplanations: 把两种策略的聚合工作都说成发生在读时，颠倒了 fan-out on write 的时机。
on read 把聚合放到读时现算；on write 把成本挪到写时先算好，读只剩一次查询——时机就是两者的本质差异。
同样把时机说反了，写时预计算被错误地描述成读时才做。
两者的本质差异是工作发生在何时，不是底层数据库品牌的选择。
optionExplanations_en: Saying both strategies aggregate at read time reverses the timing of fan-out on write.
On-read aggregates at read time; on-write moves the cost to write time so read time becomes one lookup — that timing shift is the real difference.
This also flips the timing, describing the write-time precompute as if it happened at read time instead.
The core difference is when the work happens, not which database brand sits underneath.

q: 把「发帖后 fan-out on write」的流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the fan-out-on-write flow after a user posts.
steps: Fan-out 服务查 Follows 表的 GSI（followedId 为分区键），拿到发帖人的全部粉丝
Post Service 把帖子元数据写入 Posts 表、媒体写入 S3
更新后的 feed（ZSET）写回 Redis
postId 放入队列，异步交给 Feed Fan-out 服务
为每个粉丝把新 postId 插入其预计算 feed 的头部
why: 先正常落库存媒体，然后 postId 入队异步处理：fan-out 服务反查粉丝、逐个更新预计算 feed、写回 Redis。
why_en: After the post is stored, its id goes onto a queue, and the fan-out service looks up all followers via the GSI and prepends the post to each follower's Redis feed.

flowchart LR
    P["发帖"] --> DB["Posts 表 + S3"]
