q: feed 里只有 postId，返回前要「水合」出完整帖子。有哪些可行方案？（多选）
q_en: How can a feed that only stores post IDs hydrate full posts?
options: 每个 postId 去 Posts 表查元数据——简单，但每次 feed 都多一轮数据库查询
把完整帖子元数据直接缓存进 Redis——更快，但吃内存且有一致性挑战
混合：ZSET 存 postId + 短 TTL 的元数据缓存，未命中用 BatchGetItem 批量补齐
把媒体字节也塞进 Redis 一起返回
options_en: Look up each postId against the Posts table: simple, but adds a database round trip per feed request.
Cache full post metadata directly in Redis: faster, but memory-heavy with consistency challenges.
Hybrid: ZSET stores postIds plus a short-TTL metadata cache, batch-filling misses with BatchGetItem.
Stuff the media bytes into Redis and return them too.
why: 三个选项分别是：每次回源、全量缓存、混合缓存。媒体字节永远走 S3+CDN，绝不进 Redis。
why_en: The hydration options are fetching each post from the database, caching full metadata in Redis, or a hybrid of id sets plus a short-lived metadata cache.
optionExplanations: 每次拿 postId 回源 Posts 表查元数据：实现最简单，代价是每次 feed 都多一轮数据库查询。
把完整元数据直接缓存进 Redis：读取最快，代价是吃内存、还要处理和数据库的一致性。
混合方案：ZSET 存 postId + 短时效元数据缓存，未命中用 BatchGetItem 批量补齐，兼顾速度和资源。
把媒体字节也塞进 Redis：违反了「媒体走对象存储、feed 只留轻量引用」这条分离原则。
optionExplanations_en: Look up each postId against the Posts table on every request: simplest to build, but it adds a database round trip to every feed load.
Cache the full metadata directly in Redis: fastest reads, at the cost of memory and a consistency problem against the source of truth.
Hybrid: a ZSET holds postIds plus a short-lived metadata cache, with BatchGetItem backfilling misses — balances speed against resource cost.
Stuffing media bytes into Redis too breaks the rule that media belongs in object storage and the feed only holds a lightweight reference.
scenario: feed 缓存里只存 postId，返回前要补齐 caption、作者、媒体链接，p99 预算 200ms。
scenario_en: The feed cache stores only post ids, so caption, author, and media links must be filled in within a 200ms p99 budget.

scenario: 水合方案要同时平衡读性能、内存占用和数据一致性，TTL 还要能按内存/一致性需求调节。
scenario_en: The hydration design must balance read speed, memory use, and consistency, and its TTL must be tunable.
q: 最佳方案是？
q_en: Which hydration strategy best balances speed, memory, and consistency?
options: 每次 feed 请求都对每一个 postId 分别实时查询 DynamoDB
把全部帖子的完整元数据永久驻留在 Redis 内存里不过期
把水合帖子元数据的工作完全交给客户端自己去查数据库
混合：ZSET 存 postId + 短 TTL 元数据缓存，未命中批量回填
options_en: Query DynamoDB in real time for every single postId separately on every feed request.
Keep every post's complete metadata permanently resident in Redis memory with no expiry.
Hand the entire post-metadata hydration work off to the client to query the database itself.
Hybrid: a ZSET of postIds plus a short-TTL metadata cache, batch-filling misses.
why: 混合方案兼得性能与资源：热帖元数据命中缓存，未命中批量补并回填；TTL 可按内存与一致性要求调。
why_en: The hybrid approach with an id sorted set plus a short-TTL metadata cache and batched database fills gives the best balance of speed, memory, and consistency.
whenOtherWins: 规模小的时候「每次直查 DynamoDB」最简单可靠，够用就不必额外部署一层缓存的复杂度。
tradeoff: 混合缓存的性能/内存平衡 vs 每次直查的简单可靠
optionExplanations: 每次都直查 DynamoDB：成本随并发线性上升，规模一大数据库压力和延迟都会失控。
全部元数据永久驻留内存：读最快但账单随帖子数一路涨，规模化后难以为继。
把水合工作转嫁给客户端：本该后端处理的鉴权、批量、重试全丢给了前端。
混合方案：ZSET 存 postId，短时效元数据缓存兜住热帖，未命中批量回填，有效期可按内存和一致性需求调。
optionExplanations_en: Querying DynamoDB directly on every request scales cost linearly with traffic — database load and latency both spiral at scale.
Keeping all metadata resident in memory forever gives the fastest reads, but the bill grows with post count and stops being sustainable.
Pushing hydration to the client dumps auth, batching, and retry logic — work that belongs on the backend — onto the frontend instead.
A hybrid: a ZSET holds postIds, a short-lived metadata cache covers hot posts, misses backfill in batch, and the cache lifetime can be tuned for memory vs freshness.

q: 用户修改了帖子 caption，元数据缓存怎么保持正确？
q_en: How should the metadata cache stay correct when a user edits a caption?
options: 只失效那一条帖子的元数据缓存，下次未命中时带回新值
重新对该帖子作者的所有粉丝做一次全量 fan-out，覆盖写每个人的 feed
干脆禁止用户修改已发布帖子的 caption
把整个 Redis 实例的数据全部清空
options_en: Invalidate just that post’s metadata cache entry; the next miss repopulates the new value.
Redo a full fan-out to every follower of that post’s author, overwriting each feed.
Simply forbid users from editing a caption after publishing.
Flush every bit of data out of the entire Redis instance.
why: feed 里存的是 postId，不受影响；只需失效该帖的元数据缓存，下一次水合自然读到新 caption。精确失效，代价极小。
why_en: On a caption edit you just invalidate that post's cached metadata, and the next feed request repopulates it with the fresh value.
optionExplanations: 只让那一条帖子的元数据缓存失效，下次有人刷到它时自动带回新值，代价最小。
重新给这条帖子的每个粉丝做一次全量 fan-out，成本极高且完全没必要——feed 里存的只是 postId。
禁止编辑 caption 是用产品限制回避了一个本可以靠缓存策略解决的问题。
清空整个 Redis 实例会让所有用户瞬间回源，代价远超这次改动该付的。
optionExplanations_en: Invalidating just that one post's metadata cache entry lets the next read pull the new value — the smallest possible blast radius.
Re-running full fan-out to every follower for one caption edit is hugely expensive and unnecessary — the feed only stores the postId anyway.
Banning caption edits dodges a problem that a cache-invalidation strategy already solves cleanly.
Flushing the entire Redis instance sends every user back to the database at once — a far bigger cost than this change deserves.
scenario: 用户改了已发布帖子的 caption，而这条帖子已经进了数百万粉丝的 feed 缓存。
scenario_en: A user edits the caption of a published post that has already landed in millions of followers’ cached feeds.

q: fan-out on write 换来快读的同时，最大的代价是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest cost of fan-out on write?
options: 读延迟会随用户关注的账号数与这些账号的粉丝规模增长而线性上升
写放大（名人问题）：百万粉账号发帖触发数百万次 feed 写入
存储成本会因为这次改动而明显下降，节省预算
这个方案会让分页功能彻底失效，无法翻页
options_en: Read latency rises linearly with how many accounts a user follows and how large those accounts are.
Write amplification, the celebrity problem: a million-follower post triggers millions of feed writes.
Storage cost noticeably drops and saves budget because of this change.
This approach completely breaks pagination, making it impossible to page through.
why: 读时复杂度换成了写时复杂度：粉丝越多写放大越猛。名人一条帖 = 数百万次 Redis 写，这就是必须再引入混合方案的原因。
why_en: The cost of fan-out on write is write amplification: one post by a celebrity with millions of followers triggers millions of feed writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次用户动作触发大量内部写入，例如一个名人发帖要写入数百万粉丝 feed。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One user action causes many internal writes, such as a celebrity post being written to millions of follower feeds.

scenario: 系统已经改用 fan-out on write（发帖时把 postId 预计算进每个粉丝的 feed）来保证读取够快。
scenario_en: The system now uses fan-out on write, precomputing each follower's feed when a post is created, so feed reads stay fast.
optionExplanations: 读延迟不是这次改动的代价，恰恰是它要解决的问题，方向说反了。
写放大：粉丝越多，一条帖子触发的 feed 写入就越多，百万粉账号一发帖就是数百万次写。
存储成本一般会因为要存预计算的 feed 数据而上升，不是下降。
分页机制不受这次架构改动影响，翻页逻辑照常工作。
optionExplanations_en: Read latency isn't a cost of this change — it's the exact problem the change was meant to fix, so this has the direction backwards.
Write amplification: more followers means more feed writes triggered per post, and a million-follower account turns one post into millions of writes.
Storage cost usually goes up, not down, because you are now storing precomputed feed data — this reverses the direction.
Pagination is unaffected by this change; paging logic keeps working exactly as before.

scenario: 绝大多数账号粉丝有限，极少数名人粉丝数百万；既要保住普通用户的快读，又不能让名人发帖压垮写路径。
scenario_en: Most authors have limited followers but a few celebrities have millions; the system needs fast reads for normal users without crushing the write path for celebrities.
q: 标准解法是？
q_en: What is the standard fix for the celebrity fan-out problem?
options: 不区分粉丝规模，所有作者一律走 fan-out on write，靠加机器扛住写放大
不区分粉丝规模，所有作者一律走 fan-out on read
混合：粉丝低于阈值的作者写时预计算；名人帖读时实时查询再按时间合并
用运营手段限制名人每天只能发一条帖子
options_en: Regardless of follower size, every author gets fan-out on write, absorbing write amplification by adding machines.
Regardless of follower size, every author uniformly gets fan-out on read.
Hybrid: authors below a follower threshold precompute at write time; celebrity posts are merged in at read time.
Use an operational policy limiting celebrities to one post per day.
why: 按粉丝数分流：多数人 fanout-on-write 保证快读，少数名人 fanout-on-read 控制写放大。名人发帖只写 Posts 表，不触发异步 feed 更新。
why_en: The hybrid combines fan-out on write for most users with fan-out on read for celebrity accounts, balancing fast reads against manageable write amplification.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务里根本没有超高粉账号（企业内部工具、小社区），纯 fan-out on write 更简单，犯不着维护两套系统。
tradeoff: 普通用户快读 vs 名人写放大可控
optionExplanations: 所有人都走写时预计算，名人一发帖就会触发数百万次写入，写放大没解决。
所有人都走读时聚合，普通用户的快读需求也满足不了，等于回到老问题。
按粉丝数设阈值分流：多数人写时预计算保读快，少数名人读时实时合并控制写放大。
限制名人发帖频率是运营手段，没有触碰架构本身的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Precomputing for everyone means a celebrity post triggers millions of writes — write amplification is still unsolved.
Reading everyone in real time cannot hit the fast-read bar for regular users either — that is just the old problem again.
Split by a follower-count threshold: most accounts precompute on write for fast reads, the few celebrities merge in real time on read to cap write cost.
Rate-limiting celebrity posting is a product lever, not an architectural fix for the underlying problem.

scenario: 在按粉丝数分流的混合方案里，需要定一个具体阈值来区分「名人」和普通用户，这个阈值决定了多少作者走预计算、多少作者走实时合并。
scenario_en: In the hybrid fan-out design, the team needs a concrete threshold to classify celebrity accounts and decide who gets precomputed.
q: 用来区分「名人」与普通用户的示例阈值是？
q_en: What example follower threshold separates celebrities from regular users?
options_en: One thousand followers.
Ten thousand followers.
One hundred thousand followers.
One million followers.
why: 示例阈值 10 万粉：低于它走预计算，高于它走读时合并。记住这是个要调的旋钮，不是魔法常数。
why_en: The example threshold is one hundred thousand followers, below which feeds are precomputed and above which posts are merged at read time.

q: 混合方案下，用户请求 feed 的读路径是？
q_en: In the hybrid design, what does the feed read path do?
options: 只读取 Redis 里已经预计算好的那部分非名人 feed
完全不用 Redis，每次都只实时查询 Posts 表
先返回名人帖，再单独发起一次请求补普通帖，由客户端自己拼接成完整 feed
取 Redis 预计算 feed + 实时查所关注名人的近期帖，按时间合并
options_en: Only read the already-precomputed non-celebrity portion of the feed in Redis.
Skip Redis entirely and only query the Posts table in real time, every time.
Return celebrity posts first, then a second request for ordinary posts, letting the client stitch the full feed.
Fetch the precomputed feed from Redis and merge it chronologically with a live query for followed celebrities.
why: 读路径变成「预计算 + 实时合并」：Redis 拿大头，名人帖现查现补，最后按时间序 merge。这是牺牲一点读延迟换写侧可控。
why_en: At read time the precomputed Redis feed is merged chronologically with freshly queried recent posts from any followed celebrities.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["feed 请求"] --> R["Redis:预计算 feed
(粉丝数少于 10 万的作者)"] U --> C["Posts 表:所关注名人的近期帖"] R --> M["按时间序合并"] C --> M M --> O["返回用户"]
optionExplanations: 假设所有作者都被预计算了，漏掉了名人这条实时合并分支。
假设完全没有预计算，白白丢掉了普通用户已经拿到的读性能收益。
把一次请求拆成两次响应，客户端要处理拼接和去重，体验反而变差。
取 Redis 里预计算的非名人部分，再实时查所关注名人的近期帖子，两者按时间戳合并成一份 feed 返回。
optionExplanations_en: Assumes every author is precomputed, missing the celebrity real-time-merge branch entirely.
Assumes no precompute exists at all, throwing away the read-performance win regular users already have.
Splitting one request into two responses forces the client to stitch and de-dupe them — worse experience, not better.
Pull the precomputed non-celebrity feed from Redis, query followed celebrities' recent posts live, then merge both by timestamp into one feed.
scenario: 系统已按粉丝阈值分流：普通作者写时预计算进 Redis，名人帖不做预计算。
scenario_en: The system already splits by follower threshold: ordinary authors are precomputed into Redis, celebrity posts are not.

scenario: 混合 feed 方案：普通用户发帖时预先写入粉丝 feed；粉丝特别多的账号不做全量写入，而是在读 feed 时再合并他们的新帖。阈值暂定为 10 万粉丝。
scenario_en: In the hybrid feed design, ordinary authors precompute fan-out, while high-follower authors are merged at read time. The initial threshold is 100K followers.
q: 为什么这个「名人阈值」必须仔细调？
q_en: Why must the celebrity threshold be tuned carefully?
options: 太低→更多账号读时合并，读变慢；太高→写放大未解决
这个阈值随便设一个数字就行，读写两条路径都不会因此发生改变
阈值设得越高，系统整体表现就会越好，没有代价
阈值设得越低，系统整体表现就会越好，没有代价
options_en: Too low slows reads with more read-time merging; too high leaves write amplification unsolved.
Just pick any number; neither the read nor the write path changes because of it.
The higher the threshold, the better the system performs overall, with no downside.
The lower the threshold, the better the system performs overall, with no downside.
why: 阈值太低，会把很多中等粉丝账号也当名人，导致更多 feed 请求要实时合并；阈值太高，高粉账号仍会写放大，问题没被控制住。
why_en: The celebrity threshold trades read latency against write amplification: too low creates too much read-time merging, while too high leaves high-follower write fan-out unsolved.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次用户动作触发大量内部写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One user action causes many internal writes.

optionExplanations: 阈值太低，更多中等粉丝账号被当成名人、更多请求要实时合并变慢；阈值太高，高粉账号仍走预计算，写放大没被控制住。
随便设一个数字，等于放弃了这个阈值本该做的流量调节作用。
只看到写放大这一侧，阈值调得越高读性能其实越受影响。
只看到读性能这一侧，阈值调得越低写放大问题依然存在。
optionExplanations_en: Too low, and more mid-tier accounts get treated as celebrities, so more requests fall into the slower real-time merge; too high, and high-follower accounts still precompute, so write amplification stays unsolved.
Picking the number at random throws away the whole point of having a tunable threshold.
This only sees the write-amplification side — pushing the threshold up actually hurts read performance too.
This only sees the read-performance side — pushing the threshold down leaves write amplification unresolved.

q: 混合方案给用户体验和运维带来什么副作用？
q_en: What side effects does the hybrid fan-out design create?
options: 混合方案对所有用户来说都不会带来任何体验差异
关注名人多的用户 feed 更慢、体验不一致，还多一套缓存要维护
受影响、体验变差的其实是名人自己刷 feed 的速度，普通用户不受影响
混合方案会让整条写路径彻底不可用，发帖失败
options_en: The hybrid approach causes absolutely no experience difference for any user.
Users following many celebrities get slower, inconsistent feeds, plus an extra cache layer to maintain.
It’s the celebrities’ own feed-loading speed that degrades, while ordinary users are unaffected.
The hybrid approach makes the entire write path unusable, causing posts to fail.
why: 谁关注的名人多，谁的实时合并就重——体验分层了。应对：分用户段设 SLA、给名人帖加缓存；预计算+实时两套系统并存，运维复杂度上升。
why_en: Users following many celebrities get slower feeds, so you need per-segment SLAs, extra caching for celebrity posts, and careful monitoring of two coexisting systems.
optionExplanations: 说所有用户体验完全一样，忽视了关注名人多的用户确实要多等实时合并那部分。
重度关注名人的用户会更频繁触发实时合并，体验比别人慢；后台要同时维护预计算和实时两条链路，监控和排障的工作量也上升。
受影响的是关注名人的粉丝，不是名人自己刷 feed 的体验，这里把对象搞反了。
写路径不会因为这次改动整体失效，只是名人分支不走预计算而已，说法夸大了。
optionExplanations_en: Claiming everyone's experience is identical ignores that users who follow a lot of celebrities really do wait longer for the real-time merge.
Users who follow more celebrities carry more real-time-merge weight, so the experience stratifies — and running precompute and real-time side by side means ops has two systems to watch.
It's the celebrity's followers who feel the effect, not the celebrity's own feed — this points at the wrong party.
The write path does not break outright from this change; only the celebrity branch skips precompute — this overstates the impact.
scenario: 混合 feed 已上线：普通帖走 Redis 预计算，名人帖读时实时查询再合并。
scenario_en: The hybrid feed is live: ordinary posts come from precomputed Redis, celebrity posts are queried and merged at read time.

scenario: 面试官追问：这套按粉丝数分流的混合 fan-out 方案，是不是只是理论上说得通，实际公司会不会真的这么做？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether this follower-count-based hybrid fan-out design is only theoretical or used in real systems.
q: 回答这个追问时，最有力的论据是什么？
q_en: What is the strongest evidence that the hybrid fan-out design is practical?
options: 声称 Instagram 全量预计算所有人 feed，从不对名人账号做特殊处理
声称 Instagram 全部读时实时聚合，不做任何预计算
指出 Instagram 生产环境用的就是类似的混合方案——收益大过额外复杂度
承认没有公司真的这么做，这只是面试的理论练习
options_en: Claim Instagram fully precomputes everyone's feed with no special casing even for celebrity accounts.
Claim Instagram does pure read-time aggregation with no precomputation at all.
Point out Instagram's production system uses a similar hybrid approach, where the benefit outweighs the added complexity.
Admit no real company does this; it's only an interview exercise.
why: Instagram 生产实践采用了类似混合策略，说明这套「按粉丝数分流」不是纸上谈兵。面试里可以引用它给方案背书。
why_en: Instagram itself uses a similar hybrid approach in production, showing the benefits outweigh the added complexity.
optionExplanations: 声称全量预计算所有人，正好和已知的名人写放大问题矛盾。
声称全部读时聚合，和 500ms 的延迟目标矛盾——已经证明这条路走不通。
指出 Instagram 生产环境用的就是类似的按粉丝数分流方案，说明这不是纸上谈兵，收益盖过额外复杂度。
承认没人这么做等于自己放弃了一个本可以引用的真实依据，削弱说服力。
optionExplanations_en: Claiming everything is fully precomputed contradicts the already-established celebrity write-amplification problem.
Claiming everything aggregates at read time contradicts the 500ms latency target — that path was already ruled out.
Pointing out that Instagram's production system uses a similar follower-count split shows this isn't purely theoretical — the payoff outweighs the added complexity.
Admitting no one really does this throws away a real reference point you could have cited, weakening the argument.

scenario: 发帖接口必须毫秒级返回，但一条帖子的 fan-out 可能要更新数百万粉丝的 feed，耗时很长。
scenario_en: The post API must return in milliseconds, but fan-out for one post may update millions of follower feeds.
q: 怎么处理这段长耗时工作？
q_en: How should the system handle long-running fan-out work?
options: 在发帖这一次请求里同步做完全部 fan-out 写入，写完才给客户端返回
postId 入队，由 Feed Fan-out 服务异步消费
放弃 fan-out 优化，全部退回读时聚合方案
让客户端不断轮询后端直到 fan-out 处理完成
options_en: Do all the fan-out writes synchronously inside the post request, returning to the client only when done.
Queue the postId and let a Feed Fan-out service consume it asynchronously.
Abandon the fan-out optimization and revert entirely to read-time aggregation.
Have the client keep polling the backend until fan-out finishes processing.
why: 长耗时工作放队列异步做：发帖立即返回，fan-out 后台慢慢跑。队列还附赠削峰、重试与故障隔离。
why_en: Feed fan-out is a long-running task, so the post id goes onto a queue and a worker service updates follower feeds asynchronously.
whenOtherWins: 粉丝数极小、fan-out 毫秒级完成的场景同步写也无妨，但队列的削峰与重试能力通常仍然值得。
tradeoff: 异步队列削峰 vs 同步简单直接
optionExplanations: 同步做完全部 fan-out 才返回，会把发帖延迟拖到秒级甚至更高，违反毫秒级响应的要求。
postId 入队，Feed Fan-out 服务异步消费——发帖立即返回，长任务放后台跑，还顺带拿到削峰和重试能力。
放弃 fan-out 优化直接退回读时聚合，等于把已经解决的问题又打开了。
让客户端不断轮询，多绕的网络往返和客户端复杂度都是不必要的开销。
optionExplanations_en: Doing all the fan-out synchronously before responding drags post latency to seconds or worse — violating the millisecond response bar.
Enqueue the postId and let the Feed Fan-out service consume it async — the post returns immediately, the long job runs in the background, and you get load-smoothing and retries for free.
Dropping fan-out and falling back to read-time aggregation reopens a problem that was already solved.
Making the client poll repeatedly adds network round trips and client complexity for no real benefit.

q: 把 feed 放 Redis，面试里应主动交代哪些持久性/可用性手段？（多选）
q_en: Which Redis durability and availability measures should you mention?
options: Redis Sentinel：高可用与自动故障转移
Redis Cluster：把数据分片到多个节点
AOF 或 RDB 持久化，故障后可恢复数据
把 Redis 当作永不宕机的黑盒
options_en: Redis Sentinel: high availability and automatic failover.
Redis Cluster: sharding data across multiple nodes.
AOF or RDB persistence so data can be recovered after a failure.
Treat Redis as a black box that never goes down.
why: 主动说出「AOF 持久化 + Sentinel 故障转移 + Cluster 分片」表明你考虑过 Redis 挂掉的后果，而不是把它当魔法黑盒。
why_en: Proactively mention Redis Sentinel for failover, Redis Cluster for sharding, and AOF or RDB persistence so a node failure does not wipe the feeds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控 Redis 主从节点、在主节点故障时自动切换的高可用组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Sentinel monitors Redis nodes and automatically promotes a replica if the primary fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据按哈希槽分片到多个 Redis 节点的水平扩展方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster shards data by hash slot across multiple nodes for horizontal scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的两种持久化机制：AOF 记录写命令日志，RDB 定期做内存快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF and RDB are Redis persistence mechanisms: AOF logs every write command, while RDB takes periodic memory snapshots.

optionExplanations: Sentinel 监控主从节点，主节点故障时自动切到副本，保证高可用。
Cluster 把数据按哈希槽分片到多个节点，突破单机内存和吞吐上限。
AOF 记录写命令、RDB 定期快照，两者都能在进程重启或崩溃后把数据找回来。
把 Redis 当成永不宕机的黑盒，是没考虑过故障后果的规划态度。
optionExplanations_en: Sentinel watches primary and replicas and auto-fails-over to a replica when the primary dies — the high-availability piece.
Cluster shards data across nodes by hash slot, breaking past a single node's memory and throughput ceiling.
AOF logs every write command and RDB takes periodic snapshots — either lets you recover data after a crash or restart.
Treating Redis as a black box that never goes down means you have not planned for what happens when it does.
scenario: 预计算好的 feed 只存在 Redis 内存里，节点一挂，用户 feed 会不会整体丢失。
scenario_en: The precomputed feed lives only in Redis memory, so a node failure raises the question of whether feeds are lost outright.

q: 把 feed 架构的完整决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the full feed-architecture decision chain.
steps: 选型：fan-out on write——发帖时把 postId 预计算进每个粉丝的 Redis feed
缓解：混合方案——粉丝数超过 10 万的名人不预计算，读时实时合并
需求：feed 端到端 <500ms，读写比极端（每天刷多次、偶尔发帖）
代价：名人发帖触发数百万次 feed 写入（写放大）
判断：读时聚合要上千次查询、延迟不可控，必须把计算搬到写时
why: 完整链条：需求（快读+极端读写比）→ 判断（读时算不可行）→ 选型（写时预计算）→ 代价（名人写放大）→ 缓解（阈值分流的混合方案）。
why_en: The decision chain runs from the latency requirement, to rejecting read-time aggregation, to precomputing on write, to the celebrity write-amplification cost, to the hybrid threshold mitigation.
diagram:
graph TD
    ReadSlow[Fanout on read is slow] --> Precompute[Precompute feed]
    Precompute --> WriteFanout[Fanout on write]
    WriteFanout --> CelebProblem[Celebrity write explosion]
    CelebProblem --> Hybrid[Hybrid fanout]
tradeoff: 写时预计算换快读 vs 读时聚合换简单写

q: 补全混合 fan-out 的分流规则：
q_en: Complete the hybrid fan-out routing rule.
text: 粉丝数低于 {{100,000}} 的作者发帖走 {{fan-out on write}}（预计算进每个粉丝的 feed）；超过阈值的名人帖走 {{fan-out on read}}（读 feed 时实时查询并合并）。
why: 一句话记住混合方案：小号写时展开、大号读时合并，阈值 10 万粉。它同时守住了普通用户的读延迟和名人发帖的写放大。
why_en: Authors under one hundred thousand followers get fan-out on write while celebrity posts above the threshold are fetched and merged at read time.

scenario: 产品要求支持照片和视频两种媒体类型，团队需要为上传接口定一个具体的大小上限，这个上限会决定要不要做分块上传。
scenario_en: The product supports both photos and videos, and the upload limit decides whether chunked upload is required.
q: 系统要支持的单个媒体大小上限是？
q_en: What single-media size limits must the system support?
options: 照片 2MB、视频 100MB
照片 100MB、视频 10GB
不设上限
照片最大 8MB、视频最大 4GB
options_en: Photos two megabytes, videos one hundred megabytes.
Photos one hundred megabytes, videos ten gigabytes.
No upper limit at all.
Photos up to eight megabytes, videos up to four gigabytes.
why: 照片 8MB、视频 4GB。4GB 这个数字直接触发分块上传的需求，因为它超过了单个 HTTP 请求的负载上限。
why_en: The system supports photos up to eight megabytes and videos up to four gigabytes, which forces chunked uploads.
optionExplanations: 2MB 照片和 100MB 视频低估了真实视频上传需求，会让后面的分块设计看不必要。
100MB 照片和 10GB 视频把上限放得过大，成本和滥用控制都会被放大。
不设上限无法做容量规划，也给滥用和超大请求留下缺口。
8MB 照片、4GB 视频是本题目标上限；4GB 直接要求分块上传。
optionExplanations_en: A 2MB photo and 100MB video limit underestimates real video uploads and would make chunking look unnecessary.
A 100MB photo and 10GB video limit is oversized, amplifying cost and abuse-control problems.
No upper limit makes capacity planning impossible and leaves the upload API open to abusive huge requests.
Eight megabytes for photos and four gigabytes for videos is the target here; the 4GB video limit directly forces chunked upload.

q: 为什么 4GB 视频必须分块（chunk）上传？
q_en: Why must a 4GB video be uploaded in chunks?
options: 单个 HTTP 请求负载上限通常 <2GB，4GB 视频装不下
S3 这个对象存储服务根本不接受视频文件类型的上传
DynamoDB 单条记录写不下 4GB 大小的数据字段，必须拆开写
CDN 在协议层面强制要求所有上传都必须分块
options_en: A single HTTP request payload is usually capped under 2GB, so a 4GB video does not fit.
S3 object storage simply does not accept video file type uploads at all.
A single DynamoDB record cannot hold a 4GB data field, so it must be split.
The CDN mandates that all uploads must be chunked at the protocol level.
why: 限制来自 HTTP 层：单请求负载一般 <2GB。分块还带来断点续传和并行上传的好处。
why_en: A single HTTP request is usually capped below two gigabytes, so a four-gigabyte video must be uploaded in multiple chunks.
optionExplanations: HTTP 单个请求负载通常有 <2GB 的实际上限，4GB 视频至少要拆成两个以上的请求才传得完。
S3 本就是为存大文件设计的对象存储，完全接受视频类型上传。
视频字节从来不会写进 DynamoDB，这个前提本身就不成立。
CDN 只负责分发缓存，不参与决定上传阶段要不要分块。
optionExplanations_en: A single HTTP request typically caps out around 2GB in practice, so a 4GB video needs to be split across at least two requests just to get through.
S3 is built for large objects and accepts video uploads without issue.
Video bytes never go into DynamoDB in the first place — the premise itself is false.
A CDN only handles distribution and caching; it has no say in whether an upload gets chunked.
scenario: 用户要上传一个 4GB 视频，手机网络还可能在传输途中断开。
scenario_en: A user uploads a 4GB video over a mobile connection that may drop partway through.

scenario: 用户要上传最大 4GB 的视频；如果字节流经我们的应用服务器，带宽和连接会被长时间占用。
scenario_en: A user may upload a 4GB video; routing those bytes through the app server would tie up bandwidth and connections for a long time.
q: 标准的上传方案是？
q_en: What is the standard upload design for large media?
options: 客户端把完整字节流交给 Post Service 中转到 S3，服务器全程占用连接
改用传统的 FTP 服务器来接收这类大文件上传请求
POST /posts 返回预签名 URL，客户端用 multipart 直传 S3
把一个 4GB 的完整视频拆成多个小帖子分别单独上传
options_en: The client hands the whole byte stream to the Post Service, which relays it to S3 while holding the connection open.
Switch to a traditional FTP server to receive this kind of large-file upload request.
POST /posts returns a presigned URL and the client uploads directly to S3 with multipart upload.
Split one complete four-gigabyte video across multiple smaller posts to upload separately.
why: 预签名 URL 让客户端限时、限权地直传 S3，媒体字节完全绕开应用服务器；multipart API 负责分块与重组。
why_en: The post endpoint returns a presigned URL so the client uploads chunks directly to S3 with the multipart upload API, bypassing our servers entirely.
whenOtherWins: 小文件（几十 KB 的头像）直接经服务器上传更简单，预签名+分块流程是为大文件准备的。
tradeoff: 客户端直传 S3 vs 经应用服务器中转
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant P as Post Service
    participant S as Object Storage
    participant M as Metadata DB
    C->>P: create post metadata
    P-->>C: upload URLs
    C->>S: multipart upload
    S-->>P: completion event
    P->>M: mark media ready

termDefinitions.meaning: 带签名和有效期的临时授权链接，允许客户端直接读写云存储而不经过后端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a temporary signed link that lets a client read or write cloud storage directly, bypassing the backend.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大文件切成多块并行上传，由存储服务负责重组。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multipart upload splits a large file into chunks uploaded in parallel, which the storage service reassembles.

optionExplanations: 字节先流经应用服务器再转存 S3，服务器的带宽和连接会被长时间占用，成为瓶颈。
FTP 缺现代云上传该有的安全签名和弹性扩展，早已不是标准做法。
POST /posts 先建元数据、拿一个限时签名 URL，客户端用 multipart upload 直传 S3，字节完全绕开应用服务器。
把一个视频硬拆成多条帖子记录，破坏了「一个 Post 对应一份完整媒体」这条数据模型。
optionExplanations_en: Routing bytes through the application server before storing to S3 ties up its bandwidth and connections for the whole upload — a real bottleneck.
FTP lacks the signed, time-limited security and elastic scaling a modern cloud upload needs — it isn't the standard anymore.
POST /posts first creates the metadata and hands back a time-limited signed URL, then the client does a multipart upload straight to S3 — bytes never touch the application server.
Splitting one video into several separate post records breaks the data model where one Post maps to one complete piece of media.

scenario: 客户端要不经过后端、限时安全地把媒体直传 S3，同时后端要先建好帖子元数据。
scenario_en: The client needs a time-limited safe way to upload media directly to S3, while the backend creates post metadata first.
q: 读这个 POST /posts 的请求/响应，正确的理解是？
q_en: What is the right reading of this POST /posts request and response?
options: uploadUrl 永久有效，可以收藏起来慢慢传
uploadUrl 是限时（约 1 小时）预签名 URL，客户端凭它直传 S3
媒体的实际字节已经包含在这个响应体里
上传时必须附带我们服务器的 session cookie，S3 才会接受这次写入
options_en: uploadUrl is valid forever; you can save it and upload whenever.
uploadUrl is a presigned link valid for about an hour, letting the client upload straight to S3.
The actual media bytes are already included inside this response body.
The upload must carry our server’s session cookie before S3 will accept the write.
why: 预签名 URL 自带签名与有效期（如 1 小时），S3 凭签名验证权限，无需我们的会话；到期后 URL 作废。
why_en: The response contains a presigned URL valid for about an hour that lets the client upload straight to S3 without touching our servers.
whenOtherWins: 若必须对每个字节做同步扫描或审计，才让上传经过自家服务器中转——用吞吐换控制。
tradeoff: 限时签名换安全边界 vs 经服务器中转换审计控制
optionExplanations: 假设签名链接永不失效，泄露后会长期留一个安全缺口，和限时授权的设计初衷矛盾。
uploadUrl 是约 1 小时后失效的限时预签名 URL，S3 独立校验签名和权限范围，不依赖我们的会话状态。
4GB 的媒体字节根本塞不进一个普通 JSON 响应体，技术上不现实。
S3 不认识我们自定义的会话 cookie，它的鉴权只看签名本身。
optionExplanations_en: Assuming the signed link never lapses leaves a long-lived security gap if it leaks — that contradicts the whole point of time-limited authorization.
uploadUrl is a presigned URL good for about an hour; S3 checks the signature and its scope on its own, with no dependency on our session state.
A 4GB media payload simply can't fit inside a normal JSON response body — not technically feasible.
S3 doesn't recognize our custom session cookie at all; its authorization only looks at the signature.

q: 帖子元数据里的媒体上传状态字段如何流转？
q_en: How should the media upload status in post metadata transition?
options: 创建时置 pending，传完后改 complete 并写入 object_key
创建帖子的那一刻状态字段就直接被置为 complete 状态，feed 里立即可见
完全不需要引入任何字段来追踪上传的完成状态
上传状态被保存在 S3 对象自带的元数据标签里
options_en: Set to pending at creation, then flipped to complete with the object key once the upload lands.
The status is set straight to complete the instant the post is created, so it shows in the feed immediately.
No field is needed at all to track whether the upload has completed.
The upload status is stored inside the tags that come attached to the S3 object.
why: 元数据先行、媒体后到，中间用 pending 状态占位；上传完成才补 object_key 并置 complete。feed 只应展示 complete 的帖子。
why_en: Post metadata starts with a pending upload status and is updated to complete with the S3 object key once the media upload finishes.
optionExplanations: 创建时先置为 pending 占位，媒体传完、S3 确认后再补 object_key 并改成 complete，feed 只展示 complete 的帖子。
假设元数据创建和媒体上传同一时刻完成，和预签名 URL 异步上传的真实时序不符。
不引入任何状态字段就没法区分「上传中」和「已完成」，容易展示破损内容。
把业务状态存进对象存储的标签，查询要多打一次 S3 API，效率和一致性都更差。
optionExplanations_en: Create it as pending as a placeholder, then once S3 confirms the upload, fill in object_key and flip it to complete — the feed only shows complete posts.
Assuming metadata creation and media upload finish at the same instant does not match the real async timing of a presigned-URL upload.
With no status field at all, there's no way to tell 'still uploading' from 'done,' so broken content can end up on screen.
Storing this business state as an object-storage tag instead means every check costs an extra S3 API call, and it is worse for consistency too.
scenario: 元数据先落库、媒体走预签名 URL 直传 S3，中间有几分钟没有 object_key 的空窗。
scenario_en: Metadata is written first while media goes straight to S3 by presigned URL, leaving minutes with no object key.

q: 上传完成后更新元数据：客户端驱动 vs 服务端驱动，怎么对比？
q_en: How do client-driven and server-driven metadata updates compare after upload?
options: 客户端驱动的更新方式天生就比服务端驱动更加可靠
两种驱动方式提供的一致性保障力度完全相同
服务端驱动反而比客户端驱动简单得多，几乎不用配置事件通知、权限和重试逻辑
客户端 PATCH 简单但需信任上报；S3 事件触发 Lambda 后端可控
options_en: The client-driven update approach is inherently far more reliable than server-driven.
The two driving approaches provide exactly the same strength of consistency guarantee.
Server-driven is far simpler than client-driven, needing almost no event-notification, permission, or retry setup.
A client PATCH is simple but trusts the report; an S3 event triggering Lambda keeps control in the backend.
why: 客户端驱动 = 客户端传完自己发 PATCH，简单但不可信；服务端驱动 = S3 事件通知触发后台任务自动更新，复杂但一致性有保障。
why_en: A client PATCH is simpler but trusts the client, while S3 event notifications triggering a Lambda give the backend full control, which most production systems prefer.
tradeoff: 实现简单但依赖客户端可信 vs 实现复杂但一致性有保障

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的事件触发无服务器函数，可响应 S3 等事件自动执行代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS Lambda is a serverless function that can run code automatically in response to events like an S3 upload.

optionExplanations: 把「客户端可信」直接等同于「更可靠」，忽略了客户端可能崩溃或干脆不上报。
两种方式在一致性保障力度上差距很大，说完全相同是不准确的。
只看到了实现复杂度这一半，没看到一致性保障上的明显差距。
客户端 PATCH 实现简单但要信任客户端上报；S3 事件触发 Lambda 更复杂但由后端全权掌控，一致性有保障。
optionExplanations_en: Equating 'the client is trustworthy' with 'more reliable' ignores that the client can crash or simply never report back.
The two approaches differ a lot in how strong a consistency guarantee they give — calling them identical is not accurate.
This only sees the implementation-complexity half of the picture, missing the real gap in consistency guarantees.
Client PATCH is simple to build but trusts the client to report back; an S3 event triggering Lambda is more work but keeps the backend fully in control with a real consistency guarantee.
scenario: 媒体直传 S3 后要把帖子改成 complete，但客户端的上报可能丢失，也可能被伪造。
scenario_en: After media lands in S3 the post must flip to complete, but a client-sent report can be lost or forged.

q: 把大文件上传的完整流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the complete large-file upload flow.
steps: S3 事件通知触发 Lambda/后台任务
客户端用 multipart upload 把分块直传到预签名 URL
调用 POST /posts：创建 pending 状态的帖子元数据，并拿到预签名 URL
任务把 S3 object_key 写回帖子元数据，状态置为 complete
S3 自动重组所有分块，落成最终文件
why: 先建元数据拿 URL，再分块直传，S3 重组后发事件，后台任务收尾更新状态。整条链里媒体字节从未经过应用服务器。
why_en: Create the pending post and get a presigned URL, upload chunks directly to S3, let S3 reassemble and fire an event, then a background job marks the post complete.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant PS as Post Service
    participant S3 as S3
    participant L as Lambda
    C->>PS: POST /posts (caption)
    PS-->>C: postId + 预签名URL (状态pending)
    C->>S3: multipart 分块直传
    S3->>S3: 重组分块
    S3-->>L: 上传完成事件
    L->>PS: 写入object_key、状态complete

q: 直接从 S3 给全球用户提供媒体，会撞上哪些问题？
q_en: What problems appear if global users read media directly from S3?
options: S3 这个对象存储服务根本无法用来存储图片文件
S3 的存储成本太低了，反而显得不太划算
跨洲用户延迟数秒、每次直打 S3 又贵又无缓存、且不分设备一律发高清原图
S3 这个服务完全不支持通过 HTTPS 协议传输数据，必须自建代理层转发
options_en: S3, the object storage service, cannot be used to store image files at all.
S3's storage cost is so low that it actually seems not very worthwhile.
Cross-continent users see seconds of latency, uncached direct S3 hits are costly, and every device gets the same high-res original.
S3 does not support transferring data over HTTPS at all, so you must build your own proxy layer.
why: 三宗罪：远端延迟（秒级）、无缓存导致 S3 请求成本失控、不做设备适配浪费带宽。小应用可以这么起步，全球规模必挂。
why_en: Serving straight from S3 means seconds of latency for faraway users, costly uncached requests, and the same high-resolution file for every device.
optionExplanations: S3 本来就是为图片、视频这类对象设计的存储服务，这个说法本身错了。
把成本方向说反了——真正的问题恰恰是没有缓存导致直打 S3 的请求成本失控。
跨洲用户加载要等好几秒、每次直打 S3 既贵又没有缓存兜底、还不分设备一律发高清原图浪费带宽——三个问题一起暴露。
S3 原生支持 HTTPS 传输，这个说法也是错的。
optionExplanations_en: S3 was built to store objects like images and video — this claim about it is simply wrong.
This gets the cost direction backwards — the real problem is no caching, which lets S3 request costs spiral.

Cross-continent loads take seconds, every direct hit to S3 is expensive with no caching to absorb it, and serving the same high-res original to every device wastes bandwidth — all three problems show up at once.
S3 natively supports HTTPS transfer, so this claim is also wrong.
scenario: 媒体只存 us-east-1 的 S3，用户遍布全球，手机和桌面都直接从 S3 拉原图。
scenario_en: Media sits only in S3 in us-east-1 while users are worldwide, and every phone and desktop pulls the original straight from S3.

scenario: 媒体存在 us-east-1 的 S3，新加坡用户加载一张图要等好几秒；要求全球用户毫秒级出图。
scenario_en: Media is stored in S3 in us-east-1, and a user in Singapore waits seconds for an image; global users need millisecond-level image loads.
q: 第一步改进是？
q_en: What is the first improvement for global media delivery?
options: 在 S3 前加 CDN：边缘节点就近供图，未命中再回源 S3 缓存
在每个大洲都各自复制部署一整套后端服务、数据库与对象存储，各自独立运行
什么都不改，只是提示用户耐心多等待几秒钟
把所有上传的图片统一压缩到 10KB 以下再存储
options_en: Put a CDN in front of S3: edge nodes serve nearby, falling back to S3 on a miss and caching it.
Deploy a full replica of backend services, databases, and object storage on every continent, each running independently.
Change nothing; just tell the user to patiently wait a few more seconds.
Uniformly compress every uploaded image down below ten kilobytes before storing it.
why: CDN 的全球边缘网络把媒体缓存到离用户最近的位置，未命中才回源；还能顺带做传输压缩。这是全球静态媒体分发的标准答案。
why_en: Putting a CDN like CloudFront in front of S3 caches media at edge locations near users, so the Singapore user loads from a nearby server instead of the US.
whenOtherWins: 用户集中在单一区域的内部系统，同区直读 S3 已经够快，CDN 属于多余成本。
tradeoff: 边缘缓存就近分发 vs 多区域全量复制后端

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users to cut delivery latency.

optionExplanations: 在 S3 前加 CDN，把媒体缓存到离用户最近的边缘节点，未命中才回源，这是全球静态媒体分发的标准第一步。
每个大洲都复制一整套后端和数据库，成本和一致性复杂度远超「第一步改进」该有的规模。
只是提示用户多等，完全没有解决延迟这个技术问题。
把所有图片统一压到 10KB 以下是用画质换体积，没有触碰地理距离这个根因。
optionExplanations_en: Put a CDN in front of S3 so media is cached at the edge closest to each user, falling back to S3 only on a miss — the standard first step for global static-media delivery.
Replicating a full backend and database on every continent costs and complicates far more than a 'first fix' should.
Just telling users to wait longer doesn't touch the underlying latency problem at all.
Squashing every image under 10KB trades quality for size and never addresses geographic distance, the actual root cause.

scenario: 图片上传后几乎不再变化，团队要为边缘缓存定一个 TTL，值太短会频繁回源，太长又可能展示过期版本。
scenario_en: Uploaded images are almost immutable, and the team needs an edge-cache TTL that cuts origin traffic without serving stale content too long.
q: 边缘缓存 TTL 的示例值是？
q_en: What is the example TTL for edge caching?
options: 24 小时
1 分钟
永久缓存
options_en: Twenty-four seconds.
Twenty-four hours.
One minute.
Cache forever.
why: 图片是不可变内容，可以放心在边缘缓 24 小时，大幅降低回源与延迟。缓存时长可按内容类型和热度分级配置。
why_en: Since images rarely change after upload, edge locations can cache them for about twenty-four hours.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，过期后需要重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached entry stays valid before it must be refreshed.

q: 只加 CDN（不做媒体优化）还遗留什么问题？
q_en: What problem remains if we only add a CDN without media optimization?
options: 加了 CDN 之后媒体读取速度反而会明显变慢下降
CDN 这种边缘缓存架构完全没有能力缓存视频这类大文件，只能缓存小图
加了 CDN 之后媒体上传本身的速度会跟着变慢
所有设备仍拿同一份高清文件；边缘容量有限，热门媒体可能被淘汰回源
options_en: Adding a CDN actually makes media read speed noticeably slower and worse.
A CDN’s edge cache cannot cache large files like video at all, only small images.
Adding a CDN slows down the speed of the media upload process itself.
Every device still gets the same high-res file; edge capacity is limited, so popular media can be evicted and refetched.
why: CDN 解决了「远」，没解决「不分设备」：弱网手机和光纤桌面拿同一份大文件。另外边缘容量有限，热门内容也可能被挤出去。
why_en: A plain CDN still serves the same file to every device and offers limited cache control, so popular media can get evicted and refetched from origin.
optionExplanations: CDN 明明是在加速读取，说它拖慢方向完全反了。
CDN 本身完全能缓存视频等各类媒体格式，这个说法错了。
上传路径根本不经过 CDN，它只作用于下载/分发这一侧。
带宽不按机型区分，弱网手机和光纤桌面拿到的是同一份大文件；边缘节点存不下所有内容，热帖也可能被挤下线、触发额外回源。
optionExplanations_en: A CDN speeds up reads, so claiming it slows things down gets the direction completely backwards.
A CDN can absolutely cache video and other media formats — this claim is wrong.
The upload path never touches the CDN at all — it only sits on the download/distribution side.
Every device still gets the same high-res file since there is no device adaptation, and edge capacity is limited, so even popular content can get evicted and trigger needless re-fetches from origin.
scenario: S3 前已加上 CDN，跨洲延迟解决了；但弱网手机和光纤桌面仍拿同一份文件。
scenario_en: A CDN in front of S3 fixed cross-continent latency, but a weak-network phone and a fiber desktop still get the same file.

scenario: 弱网手机用户和光纤桌面用户拿到的是同一份高分辨率原图，浪费带宽、加载又慢。
scenario_en: Weak mobile users and fast desktop users receive the same high-resolution original, wasting bandwidth and slowing loads.
q: 最有效的方案是？
q_en: What is the most effective media delivery design?
options: 把所有媒体统一降为最低画质来强行节省带宽
媒体处理服务生成多分辨率/多格式变体，CDN 按设备与网络下发
让用户在上传或播放时自己手动挑选清晰度档位，系统不做任何自动适配
移动端设备一律禁止播放任何形式的视频内容
options_en: Force every media file down to the lowest quality to save bandwidth.
A media processing service generates multi-resolution variants, and the CDN serves one per device and network.
Let users manually pick a resolution tier when uploading or playing, with no automatic adaptation.
Ban every mobile device from playing any form of video content whatsoever.
why: CDN 分发 + 动态媒体优化是终态：手机自动拿小图，桌面拿高清，视频走多码率自适应流。这是大型媒体平台的通用做法。
why_en: A media processing service generates variants per resolution and format, and the CDN serves the right one based on each device and network.
whenOtherWins: 小规模应用不值得维护变体管线——一份原图 + CDN 自带压缩已够，等带宽成本真成问题再上。
tradeoff: 多变体自适应下发 vs 单一质量一刀切
diagram:
graph LR
    Original[Original media] --> Processor[Media optimizer]
    Processor --> Thumb[Thumbnail]
    Processor --> Web[Web variant]
    Processor --> Mobile[Mobile variant]
    Thumb --> CDN
    Web --> CDN
    Mobile --> CDN
optionExplanations: 把所有媒体统一压到最低画质，光纤桌面用户也被迫承受不必要的质量损失。
媒体处理服务生成多分辨率/多格式变体，CDN 按设备与网络下发合适版本——大型媒体平台的通用做法。
把清晰度选择丢给用户手动挑，多数人根本不会主动去调，问题没被真正解决。
移动端一律禁播视频是砍掉核心功能，不是带宽优化。
optionExplanations_en: Squashing every asset to the lowest quality forces even fiber desktop users to eat quality loss they never needed.
A media-processing service generates multi-resolution, multi-format variants, and the CDN serves the right one per device and network — the standard playbook at large media platforms.
Leaving quality choice to the user to pick manually doesn't actually fix anything, since most people never bother to adjust it.
Banning video on mobile entirely guts a core feature — that's not bandwidth optimization.

q: CDN 怎么知道该发哪个媒体变体？
q_en: How does the CDN know which media variant to serve?
options: 客户端请求里带上设备信息与网络状况，CDN 据此挑变体
CDN 在多个候选变体之间随机挑一个下发
由运营人员为每一个用户手动配置该发哪个变体，写进后台白名单
由 DNS 域名解析的结果来决定发哪个变体
options_en: The client sends device and network info in the request and the CDN picks the variant.
The CDN randomly picks one variant among the candidates to serve.
Operations staff manually configure which variant each individual user gets via a backend allowlist.
The DNS resolution result determines which variant gets served.
why: 选择变体的信号来自客户端：请求携带设备类型和网络条件，CDN 按这些信息路由到对应版本。
why_en: The client includes its device and network conditions in the request so the CDN can serve the most appropriate variant.
optionExplanations: 客户端在请求里带上设备类型和网络状况，CDN 依据这些真实信号路由到对应的变体版本。
在候选变体间随机挑一个，没法保证匹配设备真实能力。
5 亿用户级别下靠人工逐个配置完全不可能落地。
DNS 只负责把域名解析成 IP，不携带设备或网络信息，和变体选择是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: The client attaches device type and network condition to the request, and the CDN routes to the matching variant based on those real signals.
Picking a random variant among the candidates can't guarantee it matches the device's actual capability.
Manually configuring this per user is a non-starter at 500M-user scale.
DNS only resolves a domain to an IP and carries no device or network information — an unrelated mechanism.
scenario: 同一张图已生成多分辨率/多格式变体，CDN 边缘要在毫秒内决定发哪一份。
scenario_en: Multiple resolution and format variants already exist for one image, and the CDN edge must pick one within milliseconds.

scenario: 一条内容眼看要爆红，预计某些地区即将出现巨大访问量，不想让第一波用户全部打回源站。
scenario_en: A piece of content is likely to go viral in certain regions, and the team wants to avoid the first wave of users all hitting origin.
q: 缓存策略上该怎么做？
q_en: What cache strategy should handle a predictable viral spike?
options: 顺其自然，等边缘节点自己按需慢慢回源填充
把边缘缓存 TTL 统一调短一些，让内容更快过期
提前预热高访问地区的边缘缓存，热门内容缓存更激进
把这条即将爆红的内容暂时从平台下架
options_en: Do nothing special; let edge nodes slowly fill from origin on their own as demand naturally arrives.
Uniformly shorten the edge cache TTL a bit, so content expires sooner.
Proactively warm edge caches in high-traffic regions, caching popular content more aggressively.
Temporarily take the about-to-go-viral content down from the platform.
why: 对可预测的爆点主动预热边缘，把回源风暴消灭在发生前；同时按热度分级缓存强度。这就是「智能缓存策略」。
why_en: For predictably viral content you proactively warm edge caches in high-viewership regions and cache popular media more aggressively.
whenOtherWins: 流量平稳、没有爆点时，被动按需缓存足矣，预热反而浪费源站带宽。
tradeoff: 主动预热避免回源风暴 vs 被动按需缓存更省资源
optionExplanations: 完全交给边缘节点被动按需回源，第一波用户会集中打向源站，可能引发回源风暴。
把有效期统一调短反而会让边缘更频繁重新回源，加重源站压力，方向反了。
提前预热预计高流量地区的边缘缓存、对热门内容缓存更激进，把回源风暴消灭在发生之前。
把即将爆红的内容下架是产品层面的妥协，没有解决底层的缓存能力问题。
optionExplanations_en: Leaving it to edge nodes to passively pull on demand means the first wave of users all hit the origin at once — a thundering-herd risk.
Uniformly shortening the cache lifetime actually makes edges reload from origin more often, adding pressure — the wrong direction.
Prewarm edge caches in the regions expecting the traffic spike and cache hot content more aggressively — kill the thundering herd before it starts.
Taking the about-to-go-viral content down is a product-level compromise that never fixes the underlying caching capability.

q: 动态媒体优化（多变体）要付出什么代价？
q_en: What cost does dynamic media optimization add?
options: 动态媒体优化管线几乎不带来额外工程代价，存储成本与上传延迟都不受影响
每个媒体要管理多个版本，存储成本与复杂度上升；转码管线还给上传加延迟
动态媒体优化会导致用户读取内容的延迟明显上升
动态媒体优化会让已有的 CDN 缓存全部失效作废
options_en: The dynamic media optimization pipeline adds essentially no engineering cost; storage and upload latency are unaffected.
Each media item now has several versions to manage, raising storage cost and complexity, and transcoding adds upload latency.
Dynamic media optimization causes users' content read latency to rise noticeably.
Dynamic media optimization invalidates every bit of the existing CDN cache.
why: 变体越多，存储和管理越贵；转码管线又拉长了上传路径。但对大规模媒体平台，这是性能与可管理性之间最划算的折中。
why_en: Multiple variants per file raise storage cost and complexity, and the processing pipeline adds upload latency that needs monitoring.
optionExplanations: 假设多变体管线是免费的，忽略了真实存在的存储和运维成本。
每份媒体要管多个版本，存储和管理成本上升；转码管线还会拉长上传路径，需要额外监控。
读取因为拿到了合适的变体反而更快，说它变慢是把方向搞反了。
CDN 缓存机制本身不受影响，只是多了几种要缓存的变体而已。
optionExplanations_en: Assuming the multi-variant pipeline is free ignores the real storage and operational cost it adds.
Every media item now needs multiple versions to manage, so storage and complexity rise; the transcoding pipeline also stretches upload latency and needs its own monitoring.
Reads actually get faster once the right variant exists — claiming they slow down reverses the direction.
The CDN caching mechanism itself is unaffected; it just has a few more variants to cache.
scenario: 每张图、每段视频都要生成多分辨率多格式变体，媒体总量按 PB 级增长。
scenario_en: Every image and video gets multiple resolution and format variants while total media grows into the petabytes.

scenario: 平均每个媒体约 2MB，平台每天产出 1 亿帖，团队要据此估算每日新增的对象存储用量。
scenario_en: Each media object averages about 2MB and the platform creates 100M posts per day, so the team estimates daily object-storage growth.
q: 按日均产出的媒体总量，这个规模应该归入哪个存储区间？
q_en: What storage bucket does daily media output fall into?
options: 约 200TB
约 2TB
约 20PB
约 200GB
options_en: About two hundred terabytes.
About two terabytes.
About twenty petabytes.
About two hundred gigabytes.
why: 100M × 2MB = 200TB/天。这个量级说明媒体存储是成本大头，为「冷数据下沉 Glacier」埋下伏笔。
why_en: One hundred million posts at about two megabytes each add up to roughly two hundred terabytes of new media per day.

scenario: 按每天新增约 200TB 媒体累计，团队要估算十年后总存储规模，判断 S3 长期是否扛得住、是否需要分层。
scenario_en: Starting from about 200TB of new media per day, the team estimates ten-year storage size to judge long-term S3 cost and tiering.
q: 十年周期累计的媒体存储总量应归入哪个数量区间？
q_en: What order of magnitude is ten years of accumulated media storage?
options: 约 750TB
约 75PB
约 750PB
约 7.5EB
options_en: About seven hundred fifty terabytes.
About seventy-five petabytes.
About seven hundred fifty petabytes.
About seven and a half exabytes.
why: 约 750PB / 10 年。S3 装得下但很贵——所以要按访问频率分层，把长期没人看的媒体移去更冷的存储。
why_en: Over ten years the media adds up to roughly seven hundred fifty petabytes, which S3 can hold but not cheaply.

scenario: 每帖元数据约 1KB，平台每天新增 1 亿帖，团队要据此估算元数据数据库每日新增的写入量。
scenario_en: Each post has about 1KB of metadata and the platform creates 100M posts per day, so the team estimates daily metadata writes.
q: 按日均新增帖子折算，元数据数据库每日新增量应归入哪个区间？
q_en: What bucket does daily metadata growth fall into?
options: 约 100TB
约 100GB
约 1GB
约 10PB
options_en: About one hundred terabytes.
About one hundred gigabytes.
About one gigabyte.
About ten petabytes.
why: 100M × 1KB = 100GB/天，比媒体小三个数量级。若 DynamoDB 成本吃紧，不常访问的元数据同样可以下移到 S3。
why_en: One hundred million posts at one kilobyte of metadata each is about one hundred gigabytes of new metadata per day.

scenario: 10 年 750PB 的 S3 账单太贵，而其中大量老媒体几乎无人访问。
scenario_en: Ten years of 750PB in S3 is expensive, and much of the old media is rarely accessed.
q: 省钱的正确姿势是？
q_en: What is the right cost-saving storage strategy?
options: 把长期没人访问的老媒体定期直接永久删除
把所有的媒体数据不加区分地统一搬进 Redis 缓存，用内存价格换读取速度
把老媒体打成 zip 压缩包但仍留在原来的存储层
把长期未访问的媒体下移到 Glacier 等更冷存储层，冷元数据同理
options_en: Periodically and permanently delete old media that nobody has accessed in a long time.
Move all media indiscriminately into the Redis cache, trading memory cost for read speed.
Zip up the old media into an archive but leave it in the original storage tier.
Move long-untouched media to a colder tier like Glacier, and do the same for cold metadata.
why: 冷热分层是通用省钱模式：访问越少的数据放越冷（越便宜）的层。媒体去 Glacier、冷元数据去 S3，热数据留在原地。
why_en: Move media that has not been accessed in a long time to colder cheaper storage like Glacier, and likewise shift cold metadata out of DynamoDB.
whenOtherWins: 如果老内容仍被频繁回看（周年回顾、经典帖回流），Glacier 的取回延迟和费用反而伤体验，应留在标准层。
tradeoff: 冷热分层省成本 vs 统一标准层保低延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: S3 的低成本冷存储层，读取延迟高但存储费用低，适合极少访问的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Glacier is S3's low-cost cold storage tier with slower retrieval but much cheaper storage for rarely accessed data.

optionExplanations: 永久删除老媒体意味着用户以后再也拿不回自己的历史内容，违背了保留用户内容的产品预期。
把持久化对象存储的数据搬进易失性内存缓存，成本方向完全反了，还有丢数据风险。
压缩后仍留在原来昂贵的存储层，账单几乎不变，没有解决层级问题。
把长期没人访问的媒体下移到 Glacier 这类更冷的存储层，冷元数据同理下移，热数据留在原地，访问越少的数据放越便宜的层。
optionExplanations_en: Permanently deleting old media means users can never get their history back — that breaks the product promise of keeping their content.
Moving data out of durable object storage into a volatile in-memory cache reverses the cost direction and adds real data-loss risk.
Compressing it but leaving it in the same expensive tier barely moves the bill — the tiering problem is still unsolved.

Move media nobody's touched in a long time down to a colder tier like Glacier, do the same for cold metadata, and leave hot data where it is — the less something is accessed, the cheaper the tier it belongs in.

q: 补全存储温度层级（由热到冷）：
q_en: Complete the storage temperature hierarchy from hot to cold.
text: 存储由热到冷、由贵到省：{{CDN}} → 缓存/内存 → {{SSD}} → {{HDD}} → {{磁带}}；不常被访问的数据往下移一层就能省钱。
why: 「越热越贵」是存储的普适规律。任何成本讨论都可以落到这条链上：找出访问频率低的数据，把它往下挪。
why_en: Storage runs hot to cold from CDN to memory to SSD to HDD to tape, and rarely accessed data can always move down a level to save money.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["CDN(最热最贵)"] --> B["缓存/内存"]
    B --> C["SSD"]
    C --> D["HDD"]
    D --> E["磁带(最冷最省)"]

q: 微服务层面的吞吐扩展怎么做？
q_en: How should stateless microservices scale throughput?
options: 靠人工全天候盯着监控面板去手动添加机器
只做垂直扩展，一路不断购买更大规格的单台机器来提高整体吞吐上限
按 CPU/内存阈值自动水平扩缩容，前置负载均衡器分发流量
部署一台超大规格的单体 Redis 扛下全部业务流量
options_en: Have someone watch the dashboard around the clock to manually add machines.
Only scale vertically, continuously buying a bigger single machine to raise the overall throughput ceiling.
Auto-scale horizontally on CPU or memory thresholds, with a load balancer in front distributing traffic.
Deploy one oversized monolithic Redis instance to absorb all business traffic.
why: 无状态微服务的标准打法：基于 CPU/内存指标自动水平扩缩，流量由每组服务前的负载均衡器分发。
why_en: Microservices scale horizontally and automatically based on CPU or memory thresholds, with an implicit load balancer in front of each scaled group.
diagram:
graph LR
    LB[Load balancer] --> Post[Post Service pool]
    LB --> Feed[Feed Service pool]
    LB --> Follow[Follow Service pool]
    Post --> DB1[(Post DB shards)]
    Feed --> Redis[(Feed cache shards)]
optionExplanations: 靠人工盯监控手动加机器，响应速度慢，流量突增时根本来不及。
只做垂直扩展一路买更大机型，终会撞上单机硬件的物理上限。
监控指标一超阈值就自动加减实例，每组服务前配一层均衡器把请求摊开，扩缩容不需要人工介入。
让单个超大规格 Redis 扛全部业务流量，不满足分布式、高可用的基本要求。
optionExplanations_en: Relying on a human watching a dashboard to manually add machines is slow and cannot keep up with a sudden traffic spike.
Scaling only vertically by buying bigger and bigger boxes eventually hits the physical ceiling of a single machine.
Auto-scale horizontally on CPU/memory thresholds with a load balancer in front of each service group distributing traffic — the standard playbook for stateless microservices.
Putting all traffic on one giant Redis instance fails the basic bar of being distributed and highly available.
scenario: 无状态的 Post/Feed 服务白天流量是夜间的 5 倍，吞吐必须自动跟随流量。
scenario_en: The stateless Post and Feed services see five times more traffic by day than by night, so throughput must track load automatically.

scenario: 面试官在 Instagram 系统设计面试里，对中级（mid-level）和高级（senior）候选人打分标准不同，主要看候选人在 feed 生成和媒体分发这两个深挖点上的表现。
scenario_en: In an Instagram system design interview, mid-level and senior candidates are judged differently, especially on feed generation and media delivery deep dives.
q: 中级和高级候选人的期望差异体现在哪？
q_en: How do expectations differ between mid-level and senior candidates?
options: 中级：给出可用高层设计，提示下能演进；高级：主动讲清 fan-out 权衡
中级候选人必须在面试现场手写出可直接上线部署的生产级完整代码
系统设计面试对中级和高级候选人的期望标准完全一样，毫无区别
高级候选人完全不需要理解 feed 生成这个环节，只要关注媒体分发就够了
options_en: Mid-level: a workable high-level design that evolves with hints; senior: proactively explains fan-out trade-offs.
Mid-level candidates must handwrite complete, deployable, production-ready code live in the interview.
The system design interview holds mid-level and senior candidates to exactly the same bar, with no distinction at all.
Senior candidates do not need to understand feed generation at all; caring about media delivery is enough.
why: 分水岭在「要不要提示」和深度：中级借提示改进即可；高级要自己驾驭 fan-out 权衡、名人混合方案、媒体上传与索引策略。
why_en: Mid-level candidates may need hints to evolve past fan-out on read, while seniors must independently master the fan-out trade-offs, the celebrity problem, and media handling.
optionExplanations: 分水岭在要不要提示、以及讲多深：中级借提示就能改进方案，高级要主动讲清 fan-out 权衡和选型论证。
要求现场手写可上线的生产代码，混淆了系统设计轮和手写代码轮这两种考察形式。
说两个级别期望完全一样，忽视了面试官对不同级别设定的真实差异化标准。
说高级候选人不需要懂 feed 生成，恰恰说反了——这正是这道题的核心深挖点。
optionExplanations_en: The dividing line is whether hints are needed and how deep the discussion goes: mid-level can improve with a nudge, senior is expected to walk through the fan-out tradeoffs and justify the choice unprompted.
Expecting shippable production code on the spot confuses a system-design round with a coding round — different formats, different bars.
Claiming both levels are held to the exact same standard ignores that interviewers deliberately calibrate expectations by level.
Saying senior candidates don't need to understand feed generation gets it backwards — that's precisely this problem's core deep-dive.

scenario: 面试官对 Staff+ 候选人的评估重点，不是知识覆盖面，而是工程判断力：能不能在有限时间里抓住这道题真正的瓶颈。
scenario_en: For Staff+ candidates, the interviewer is testing engineering judgment, not breadth of memorized facts: can they find the real bottleneck under time pressure?
q: Staff+ 候选人在这道题上被考察什么？
q_en: What is a Staff+ candidate being evaluated on in this Instagram design question?
options: 要求候选人把所有 AWS 服务的具体名字都背得滚瓜烂熟
一开始就直接跳到设计最复杂、最重的分布式系统架构，把复杂度前置
只需要在白板上画出几个高层级的框图就已经足够了
快速锁定真正瓶颈、讲清规模演化路径、预判故障与运维问题
options_en: Requiring the candidate to have every single AWS service name memorized cold.
Jump straight to the heaviest, most complex distributed architecture from minute one, front-loading complexity.
Sketching just a few high-level boxes on the whiteboard is already enough.
Quickly locate the real bottleneck, narrate the scale-evolution path, and anticipate failure and ops issues.
why: Staff 的信号是判断力：识别真瓶颈、按规模演化设计、复杂度只花在刀刃上，同时预判故障与运维成本。过早堆复杂度反而是减分项。
why_en: Staff candidates must quickly identify the real bottlenecks, articulate how the design evolves from one million to five hundred million users, and know when simpler solutions suffice.
optionExplanations: 要求背熟所有 AWS 服务名，考的是记忆量，不是工程判断力。
一上来就堆最复杂的分布式架构，是常见的过度设计反模式。
只画高层框图，没有配瓶颈分析、容量估算和故障处理，撑不起 Staff 级别的深度。
快速锁定真正的瓶颈、讲清楚方案怎么随规模演化、知道什么时候该升级，同时预判故障和运维成本。
optionExplanations_en: Requiring memorized AWS service names tests recall, not engineering judgment.
Jumping straight to the most complex distributed architecture is a classic over-engineering anti-pattern.
A high-level box diagram alone, without bottleneck analysis, capacity estimates, or failure handling, does not carry staff-level depth.
Quickly zero in on the actual bottleneck, explain how the design evolves with scale, know when to escalate complexity, and anticipate failure modes and operational cost.

scenario: 5 亿 DAU 的 Instagram 改用 fan-out on write：发帖时就把 postId 预写进每个粉丝的 feed，读 feed 必须是一次快操作、取回按时间排序的 top N。
scenario_en: Instagram (500M DAU) switches to fan-out on write: on posting, the postId is precomputed into each follower's feed, and reading a feed must be one fast op returning the top N in time order.
q: 预计算好的 feed 该存在哪种存储里？
q_en: Which storage should hold the precomputed feed?
options: Redis 排序集（ZSET）：feed 在内存，一次取回 top N
DynamoDB 专门 Feeds 表：天然落盘、故障不丢，所以直接选它
关系型库每次请求实时 JOIN 算 feed，不预存结构
S3 给每个用户存一份 feed JSON，请求时整份拉取
options_en: A Redis sorted set (ZSET): the feed lives in memory, top N in one op.
A dedicated DynamoDB Feeds table: it persists to disk and survives failures, so just pick it.
A relational DB that JOINs to compute the feed live on every request, storing no structure.
S3 holding one feed JSON per user, pulled in full on each request.
why: feed 每次打开都读、且要一次取回按时间排序的 top N，Redis 内存态 ZSET 读写最快，直接压进 500ms 读预算。代价：内存态易失，得配 AOF/Sentinel 才不丢 feed。
why_en: A feed is read on every open and must return the sorted top N in one op, so an in-memory Redis ZSET is fastest and fits the 500ms read budget, at the cost of needing AOF and Sentinel so feeds survive a crash.
whenOtherWins: 若不想为持久性额外跑 Sentinel/AOF、又能接受略高的读延迟，专门的 DynamoDB Feeds 表把 feed 落盘、节点故障不丢，反而更省心。
tradeoff: 内存 ZSET 极速读写 vs DynamoDB Feeds 表天然持久

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，成员按分数(如时间戳)排序，取 top N 是一次 O(logN) 操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ZSET is a Redis sorted set whose members are ordered by a score such as a timestamp, so fetching the top N is a single O(logN) operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档库，天然持久化、按吞吐量水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed NoSQL key-value store that persists to disk and scales horizontally by provisioned throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 把每条写命令追加到磁盘日志，崩溃后可重放恢复数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF makes Redis append every write command to an on-disk log so data can be replayed and recovered after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的高可用组件，监控主节点并在故障时自动切换到从节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sentinel is Redis's high-availability component that monitors the primary and automatically fails over to a replica.

optionExplanations: ZSET 常驻内存，取 top N 是一次 O(logN) 操作，无需二次聚合。
持久化的专用 feed 表，故障不丢；当持久性比极致读延迟更重要时更合适，但单次读比内存慢。
这是 fan-out on read 的实时聚合，不是「存」好的 feed，5 亿 DAU 下聚合读会拖垮延迟。
对象存储适合冷数据大文件；每次整份拉 JSON 再反序列化，扛不住热点 feed 的高频小读。
optionExplanations_en: A ZSET stays in memory and fetching the top N is one O(logN) op with no second aggregation.
A durable feed table loses nothing on failure and wins when persistence matters more than raw latency, but a single read is slower than memory.
That is live fan-out-on-read aggregation, not a stored feed; at 500M DAU the aggregate read blows the latency budget.
Object storage suits cold large files; pulling a whole JSON and deserializing it per request cannot serve the high-frequency small reads of a hot feed.

scenario: Instagram HLD 阶段：读 feed 要先查 Follow 表拿关注列表，再聚合这些人的近期帖子；发帖和读 feed 都要用到帖子数据。
scenario_en: Instagram HLD stage: reading a feed first queries the Follow table for the followed list, then aggregates their recent posts; both posting and feed reads touch post data.
q: feed 生成逻辑放哪个服务？
q_en: Which service should own feed-generation logic?
options: 先放进 Post Service：feed 读依赖帖子数据，省一层服务
立刻拆出独立 Feed Service：微服务就该一功能一服务
放进 Follow Service：feed 第一步就是查用户的关注关系
放进 API Gateway：让网关直接聚合各表，少一跳
options_en: Keep it in the Post Service: feed reads depend on post data, saving a service.
Split out a dedicated Feed Service immediately — one feature, one microservice.
Put it in the Follow Service, since a feed first queries the user's follow relationships.
Put it in the API Gateway so the gateway aggregates the tables directly, saving a hop.
why: 现阶段 feed 读与帖子数据强耦合、流量还没大到要独立伸缩，放 Post Service 省掉一个服务和一次网络跳。代价：日后 feed 流量与发帖分化时得再拆分。
why_en: For now feed reads are tightly coupled to post data and traffic is not yet large enough to scale separately, so keeping it in the Post Service saves a service and a network hop, at the cost of having to split it out later once feed and posting traffic diverge.
whenOtherWins: 当 feed 读流量与发帖流量明显分化、要各自独立扩容或独立发布节奏时，拆出专门 Feed Service 才值回它的运维成本。
tradeoff: 少一层服务(系统更简单) vs 独立 Feed Service(可独立伸缩，运维成本升)

termDefinitions.meaning: 把系统拆成多个各自部署、各自伸缩的小服务，每个负责一块业务能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Microservices split a system into small independently deployed and scaled services, each owning one business capability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有客户端请求的统一入口，负责路由、认证、限流，通常不放业务聚合逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API Gateway is the single entry point for client requests, handling routing, auth, and rate limiting, and usually not business aggregation logic.

optionExplanations: 读 feed 依赖帖子元数据，与发帖同属一个域；流量未分化时合并可省一次网络往返。
「一功能一服务」是教条；本阶段耦合自然、流量未分化，多一个服务只增系统复杂度。
Follow Service 只提供第一步的关注列表；把聚合塞进它会让它越权持有帖子读逻辑。
API Gateway 该做路由/认证/限流，塞业务聚合会让网关变胖、难独立演进。
optionExplanations_en: Reading a feed depends on post metadata and belongs to the same domain as posting; while traffic has not diverged, merging saves a network round-trip.
"One feature, one service" is dogma; here coupling is natural and traffic has not diverged, so an extra service only adds system complexity.
The Follow Service only supplies the first-step followed list; pushing aggregation into it makes it overreach into post-read logic.
An API Gateway should route, auth, and rate-limit; stuffing aggregation in bloats it and blocks independent evolution.
